frame.hint: I will call you again in one hour with more news. You can call me anytime.

activities.model: Good morning. This is Fernando from Racional Engenharia, the Contract Manager on the hospital site. We had a small incident this morning on the construction site. First, the most important thing: everyone is safe and no one is hurt. We stopped the work and we isolated the area. Our team is here now to assess the situation. I will call you again in one hour with more news.

wrapUp.prompt: Agora faça o pitch ao professor, em voz alta, sem ler o modelo. Fale como se estivesse ligando para o cliente do hospital.
wrapUp.model: Hello, this is Fernando from Racional. We had an incident on the site, but everyone is safe. We stopped the work and isolated the area. The team is assessing it now. I will update you in one hour.
wrapUp.teacherNote: Foque na calma e na ordem dos passos: primeiro segurança das pessoas, depois ação, depois próximo passo. Corrija a pronúncia de 'incident', 'isolate' e 'assess'.

activities.intro: Você está numa mini-reunião de emergência com o cliente (Hospital) e a equipe de segurança da obra. Use as funções abaixo para acompanhar e participar da reunião sobre o incidente.

functions.label: acompanhar
phrases: Okay, I understand.
Let me write that down.

functions.label: pedir esclarecimento
phrases: Sorry, can you say that again?
What do you mean by 'the area'?

functions.label: confirmar
phrases: Yes, everyone is safe.
That is correct, the work is stopped.

functions.label: opinar
phrases: I think we need to isolate the area first.
In my opinion, the client must know now.

functions.label: interagir
phrases: What do you think?
Do you agree with me?

activities.task: Simule uma mini-reunião de 3 minutos sobre o incidente na obra do hospital. O professor é o cliente americano e pergunta: 'Is everyone safe?', 'What did you do?', 'When can the work start again?'. Fernando responde como Gerente de Contrato usando as frases das funções.

wrapUp.prompt: Conte ao professor, em inglês, o que ficou decidido na reunião (3 frases).
wrapUp.model: In the meeting, we confirmed that everyone is safe. We decided to keep the area isolated today. We will assess the site tomorrow and then start the work again.
wrapUp.teacherNote: Verifique se Fernando usa pelo menos uma frase de cada função. Reforce 'everyone is safe' e 'the work is stopped'.

image.alt: A construction site with workers and machines.

activities.instruction: Olhe a foto de uma obra. Imagine que aconteceu um incidente nesse lugar. Responda em inglês simples (A1+), sempre pensando no papel de Fernando como Gerente de Contrato da Racional.
questions: What do you see in the picture?
Is this a construction site?
How many workers can you see?
Is the area safe?
Where is the incident?
Who do you call first?
Do you stop the work?
What do you say to the client?

wrapUp.prompt: Descreva a cena ao professor em 3 ou 4 frases, em inglês simples, como se fosse a obra do hospital da Racional.
wrapUp.model: This is a construction site, like our hospital project. I can see workers and machines. There was an incident here, but everyone is safe. I stopped the work and I called the client.
wrapUp.teacherNote: Aceite frases curtas. Incentive o uso do vocabulário da aula: 'incident', 'safe', 'stop the work', 'isolate the area'.

lessons.title: Leading change in long projects
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você anunciará e conduzirá, em inglês simples, uma mudança importante em um projeto longo — explicando o motivo, o que muda e o apoio que você dá à equipe.
lessons.overview:
Big projects bring change. A data center for an American client can take 18 to 24 months. In so much time, the scope can change, the client can move the deadline, and the team can change too. At Racional, leading a project means leading change every week.

People do not resist change because they are bad. They resist because they do not know why. So a good contract manager explains the why first, and the what after. This is important on the construction site, where one new decision changes the work of many people.

When you lead change well, the team stays calm and the project stays on track. You say the reason, you say the new plan, and you say "I am here to support you." This is the right move, and it builds trust with your team and with the client.
lessons.intro:
Nesta prática você vai treinar como anunciar uma mudança. Lembre destas três frases-âncora: 1) o porquê — "The client moved the deadline, so we need to adapt." 2) o que muda — "From now on, we will work in two shifts." 3) o apoio — "I am here to support you."

Regra de ouro: explique o porquê antes do o quê.
lessons.situation: O cliente americano antecipou a entrega de uma fase do data center. Você precisa anunciar à equipe que a obra passará a operar em dois turnos, e há resistência.
lessons.context: Team, I want to be honest with you. The client moved the deadline, so we need to adapt. From now on, we will work in two shifts. I know this is a big change. It is not easy. But it is the right move, and I am here to support you.

vocab.example: This is a big change for the team.
Part of my job is to lead change.
We need to adapt to the new plan.
We will work in two shifts.
There is some resistance from the team.
I am here to support you.
This is the right move for the project.
From now on, we start at six.
We will roll out the new plan next week.
I want to reassure the team.
The transition will take two weeks.

exercises.title: 1. Ligue o termo à tradução
exercises.explanation: Estes quatro termos são a base para anunciar uma mudança de plano na obra.

exercises.title: 2. Como anunciar a mudança
exercises.prompt: A equipe vai resistir a dois turnos. Qual é a melhor forma de começar o anúncio?

options.text: From tomorrow you work two shifts. No questions.
options.whyWrong: Dar a regra sem o motivo gera resistência. As pessoas precisam entender o porquê primeiro.

options.text: The client moved the deadline, so we need to adapt. Here is the change.
I am not happy about this, but it is not my fault.
options.whyWrong: Se distanciar da decisão tira a sua força de líder. Você lidera a mudança, não reclama dela.

exercises.explanation: Explique o porquê antes do o quê. Quando a equipe entende o motivo, aceita melhor a mudança.

exercises.title: 3. Reconheça e siga
exercises.prompt: I know this is a big change, but it is the right ___.
exercises.explanation: 'The right move' = a decisão certa. Reconhecer a dificuldade e afirmar que é o certo é uma fala forte de líder.

commonErrors.way: 'Right way' soa diferente; a expressão de decisão é 'the right move'.

exercises.title: 4. Escreva o anúncio
exercises.prompt: Escreva 2 ou 3 frases anunciando à equipe que a obra terá dois turnos porque o cliente antecipou o prazo. Use ao menos 2 termos da aula em inglês.
exercises.modelAnswer: Team, the client moved the deadline. So from now on, we will work in two shifts. I know it is a big change, but I am here to support you.
exercises.explanation: A correção olha só o uso dos termos da aula. Comece sempre pelo porquê.

exercises.title: 5. Fale a mudança em voz alta
exercises.targetText: I know this is a big change, but it is the right move. I am here to support you.
exercises.translation: Eu sei que é uma grande mudança, mas é a decisão certa. Estou aqui para apoiar vocês.
exercises.prompt: Você está na frente da equipe. Fale com calma e firmeza, como um líder.
exercises.explanation: Tom calmo e firme. Reconhecer a dificuldade e oferecer apoio tranquiliza a equipe.

lessons.critical: Em voz alta, por 15 a 20 segundos, anuncie à sua equipe que a obra passará a operar em dois turnos. Diga o porquê, o que muda e que você está ali para apoiar.
takeaways: I can explain why we need to change.
I can announce a new plan to my team.
I can say that I support my team.
I can talk about a deadline and a shift.

teacher.overview: M1 — Desenvolver vocabulário e fluência para a atuação do gerente de contrato como líder de equipe — coordenação de coordenadores e gerentes de área, condução de feedback, reporting par…

flow.how: Aluno reconta em inglês, em 60s, o que praticou na aula anterior.
Frase-base fixa; troque um elemento por vez (cliente, prazo, valor), oralmente.
Só voz, sem ver o rosto — treina clareza.
Aplique o alvo a uma situação real do projeto do aluno.

flow.what: Fechamento · O que eu aprendi nessa lição
flow.how: Feche SEMPRE por aqui: o aluno marca cada 'I can…' que já consegue dizer em voz alta. Ao marcar todos, a aula fica registrada como concluída e mais clara no programa. É assim que toda aula termina.

watch: Priorize a FALA: o aluno deve falar na maior parte da aula.
Varie a dinâmica a cada aula — o roteiro acima rotaciona para não repetir.
teacher.richNote: Esta aula tem conteúdo interativo completo na plataforma (vocabulário, exercícios e recap).

practiceBank.title: Anunciando os dois turnos para a equipe
practiceBank.how: O aluno é o gerente da obra do data center e anuncia ao professor (que faz o pedreiro/encarregado) que a obra passa a operar em dois turnos. O aluno deve usar 'from now on', 'shift', 'the right move' e 'to reassure'. Professor reage com resistência e cobra clareza. Foco: anunciar a mudança com motivo, o que muda e o apoio dado.

practiceBank.title: Mensagem de vídeo: por que mudamos
practiceBank.how: O aluno grava 60 segundos como se fosse um vídeo interno para a equipe explicando por que o cliente americano antecipou a fase e por que isso é 'the right move'. Deve usar 'scope', 'deadline', 'to adapt' e 'transition'. Professor ouve depois e dá um feedback de clareza e fluência.

practiceBank.title: Reunião de kickoff do segundo turno
practiceBank.how: Simula-se uma reunião curta onde o aluno conduz a transição para dois turnos. O aluno fala pelo menos 4 vezes usando 'to roll out', 'transition', 'to support' e 'to be on board'. Professor entra como dois colaboradores com dúvidas diferentes; o aluno PRODUZ as respostas e fecha pedindo apoio.

practiceBank.title: Quebrando a resistência
practiceBank.how: O professor levanta objeções fortes ('a equipe não vai aceitar', 'o prazo é impossível') e o aluno deve responder defendendo a mudança com 'resistance', 'to reassure', 'to support' e 'the right move'. O aluno PRODUZ argumentos e mantém a calma. Professor pressiona para gerar fala espontânea.

practiceBank.title: Perguntas rápidas sobre a mudança
practiceBank.how: Professor e aluno alternam perguntas rápidas sobre o que muda na obra ('What changes from now on?', 'Who is on board?'). Cada resposta do aluno deve conter uma palavra-alvo: 'shift', 'scope', 'deadline', 'to adapt'. Ritmo acelerado para automatizar o vocabulário estudado.

practiceBank.title: 30 segundos para o diretor
practiceBank.how: O aluno tem 30 segundos para convencer o diretor (professor) de que liderar a mudança para dois turnos é 'the right move'. Deve abrir com o motivo, dizer o que muda e como vai apoiar a equipe, usando 'to lead change', 'to roll out' e 'to reassure'. Repete tentando ser mais direto na 2a vez.

practiceBank.title: Como conduzi uma mudança difícil
practiceBank.how: O aluno reconta, em voz alta, uma mudança real que já liderou em obra (ou inventada no data center), narrando início, resistência e desfecho. Deve usar 'to lead change', 'to adapt', 'resistance', 'transition' e 'to be on board'. Professor pede detalhes para alongar a narrativa.

practiceBank.title: O que comunicar primeiro
practiceBank.how: Apresentam-se 5 pontos do anúncio (motivo, novo prazo, turnos, apoio, próximos passos). O aluno ordena do mais importante ao menos e justifica cada escolha em inglês, usando 'deadline', 'shift', 'to support' e 'the right move'. Professor desafia a ordem para gerar mais argumentação.

practiceBank.title: Gerente na berlinda
practiceBank.how: O aluno senta na 'cadeira quente' como gerente que acabou de anunciar a mudança; professor e perguntas fictícias da equipe disparam questões difíceis sobre prazo e carga de trabalho. O aluno responde sem preparo usando 'to reassure', 'to be on board', 'from now on'. Gera fluência sob pressão.

practiceBank.title: De passado para 'from now on'
practiceBank.how: Professor diz uma frase no modo antigo ('We worked one shift') e o aluno transforma oralmente para o novo cenário usando 'from now on we...' com 'shift', 'to roll out', 'to adapt'. Drill rápido para fixar a estrutura de anunciar mudança. 8-10 transformações encadeadas.

practiceBank.title: Encarregado se recusa a aceitar o turno da noite
practiceBank.how: Cenário: um encarregado-chave (professor) não quer o turno da noite. O aluno deve negociar e conduzir a transição mantendo a pessoa 'on board', usando 'to support', 'to reassure', 'resistance' e 'transition'. O aluno PRODUZ a solução falada. Professor só cede se for bem convencido.

practiceBank.title: Um minuto sobre liderar mudança
practiceBank.how: O aluno fala 60 segundos sem parar sobre 'leading change in long projects' no data center, encaixando o máximo de vocábulo-alvo ('to lead change', 'to adapt', 'scope', 'deadline', 'transition'). Professor cronometra e marca pausas longas. Objetivo: fluência contínua.

pill.tip: Depois de som surdo (p, t, k, f), o '-s' soa como /s/: 'works', 'reports', 'meets'. Som de cobra, sem voz.
pill.sample: He works on the reports and meets the deadline.

lessons.title: Executive presence for project managers
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você falará com presença executiva em inglês simples — indo direto ao ponto, sendo claro e breve, e dizendo onde o projeto está.
lessons.overview:
Executive presence is how you come across when you speak. It is not about big words. It is about being clear and brief. A good contract manager gets to the point fast and says where the project stands.

American clients like this style a lot. In a meeting about a Racional data center, the client does not want a long story. The client wants the bottom line: are we on track or not? You give the answer first, and the details after.

You can build presence with simple habits. You pause before you speak. You cover only what matters. You give a clear recommendation. This makes the client trust you, even when your English is simple. Confidence comes from being clear, not from being perfect.
lessons.intro:
Nesta prática você vai treinar como soar claro e seguro. Lembre destas frases-âncora: "Let me get to the point." / "Here is where we stand." / "The bottom line is, we are on track."

Regra de ouro: a resposta primeiro, os detalhes depois.
lessons.situation: Em uma call de status com o cliente americano, ele tem pouco tempo. Você precisa dizer onde a obra está, de forma curta e clara.
lessons.context: Thanks for the time. Let me get to the point. Here is where we stand. The structure is on track. We are two days ahead. The bottom line is, we will deliver on time. I have one recommendation, and then we can take your questions.

vocab.example: Let me get to the point.
I want to come across as clear.
Take your time with the answer.
A calm voice holds the room.

exercises.title: 1. Ouça e escreva
exercises.correctText: Let me get to the point.
exercises.explanation: Esta é a frase clássica para começar com presença executiva: ir direto ao ponto.

exercises.title: 2. Monte a frase
exercises.explanation: 'Here is where we stand' = aqui está onde estamos. Frase forte para abrir o status da obra.

exercises.title: 3. Complete a conclusão
exercises.prompt: The bottom ___ is, we are on track.
exercises.explanation: 'Bottom line' = a conclusão, o que mais importa. O cliente americano quer ouvir isso primeiro.

commonErrors.point: Aqui a expressão fixa é 'bottom line', não 'bottom point'.

exercises.title: 4. Presença executiva na call
exercises.prompt: O cliente americano tem 10 minutos. Como você começa o status?

options.text: Well, it is a long story, let me start from the beginning.
options.whyWrong: Começar com uma história longa cansa o cliente. Ele quer a conclusão primeiro.

options.text: Let me get to the point. The bottom line is, we are on track.
I am not sure, maybe we are on track, I think.
options.whyWrong: Soar inseguro tira a sua presença. Seja claro, mesmo com inglês simples.

exercises.explanation: Presença executiva é ser claro e breve. A resposta primeiro, os detalhes depois.

exercises.title: 5. Abra o status em voz alta
exercises.targetText: Let me get to the point. The bottom line is, we are on track.
exercises.translation: Deixe-me ir direto ao ponto. O que importa é: estamos no prazo.
exercises.prompt: Você abre uma call de status. Faça uma pausa curta, respire e fale com firmeza.
exercises.explanation: Pause antes de falar. Voz calma e frase curta passam segurança.

lessons.critical: Em voz alta, por 15 a 20 segundos, abra uma call de status com o cliente americano. Vá direto ao ponto, diga onde a obra está e dê uma recomendação curta.
takeaways: I can get to the point fast.
I can say where the project stands.
I can give the bottom line first.
I can sound clear and brief.
I can speak with confidence.

teacher.overview: M1 — Desenvolver vocabulário e fluência para a atuação do gerente de contrato como líder de equipe — coordenação de coordenadores e gerentes de área, condução de feedback, reporting par…

flow.how: Em pé, repetição coral das frases-chave; acelere o ritmo a cada rodada.
Construa a frase de trás para frente, repetindo em blocos até a frase inteira.
Aluno conta um caso real da obra usando o vocabulário da aula.
Grave 60s para o portfólio de fala do aluno.

flow.what: Fechamento · O que eu aprendi nessa lição
flow.how: Feche SEMPRE por aqui: o aluno marca cada 'I can…' que já consegue dizer em voz alta. Ao marcar todos, a aula fica registrada como concluída e mais clara no programa. É assim que toda aula termina.

watch: Priorize a FALA: o aluno deve falar na maior parte da aula.
Varie a dinâmica a cada aula — o roteiro acima rotaciona para não repetir.
teacher.richNote: Esta aula tem conteúdo interativo completo na plataforma (vocabulário, exercícios e recap).

practiceBank.title: 60 segundos com o cliente sem tempo
practiceBank.how: Simula-se uma call de áudio: o cliente americano (professor) diz que tem só 1 minuto. O aluno deve dizer 'where we stand' do data center de forma curta, abrindo com 'bottom line' e fechando com uma 'recommendation'. Foco em 'to get to the point', 'clear', 'brief'. Professor interrompe se o aluno enrolar.

practiceBank.title: Cortando a gordura da frase
practiceBank.how: Professor diz uma frase longa e cheia de rodeios; o aluno a reformula curta e direta, começando por 'Bottom line...' ou 'Where we stand is...'. Drill para praticar 'to get to the point', 'brief', 'clear'. 8 frases encadeadas, cada vez mais enxutas.

practiceBank.title: Status em uma frase
practiceBank.how: O aluno resume o status da obra em UMA frase de impacto que mostre presença executiva, usando 'on track', 'bottom line' e 'where we stand'. Repete 3 vezes refinando. Professor avalia se a mensagem soa confiante e 'comes across as' clara.

practiceBank.title: Presença executiva: nato ou treinável?
practiceBank.how: Aluno e professor debatem se 'executive presence' se aprende ou já se nasce com ela. O aluno deve dar opinião e justificar usando 'confidence', 'to come across as', 'to hold the room'. Professor assume o lado oposto para forçar argumentação falada.

practiceBank.title: Cliente com 90 segundos no relógio
practiceBank.how: O aluno está na call e o professor (cliente) dispara: 'Give me the bottom line, I have 90 seconds.' O aluno deve cobrir status, risco e recomendação sem preparo, usando 'to cover', 'recommendation', 'where we stand'. Treina presença sob pressão de tempo.

practiceBank.title: Áudio executivo de update
practiceBank.how: O aluno grava um áudio de 60s de update do projeto como se mandasse ao cliente, indo direto ao ponto. Deve usar 'on track', 'to cover', 'bottom line', 'recommendation'. Ao ouvir, professor marca onde houve enrolação e o aluno regrava mais 'brief'.

practiceBank.title: Frases que NÃO soam executivas
practiceBank.how: Professor lê frases vagas ou inseguras ('I think maybe we are sort of okay...'). O aluno corrige em voz alta para soar com presença, usando 'clear', 'confidence', 'to come across as'. Quem corrige mais frases em 5 min vence. Foca em fala assertiva.

practiceBank.title: O aluno cobra presença
practiceBank.how: Inverte-se: o aluno faz o cliente americano impaciente e o professor dá um status ruim (cheio de rodeios). O aluno deve interromper e exigir 'to get to the point' e 'where we stand'. Praticar o vocabulário pelo ângulo de quem cobra clareza.

practiceBank.title: Falar 60s sobre o data center sem hesitar
practiceBank.how: O aluno fala 60 segundos contínuos sobre onde o projeto está, sem 'ééé' nem pausas longas, demonstrando 'to hold the room'. Usa 'on track', 'where we stand', 'to cover'. Professor cronometra e reinicia se houver pausa longa. Treina confiança e fluência.

practiceBank.title: Abrir a reunião com presença
practiceBank.how: O aluno abre uma reunião de status de 2 minutos: cumprimenta, diz o que vai 'cover', dá o 'bottom line' e pausa para perguntas ('to pause'). Professor age como dois stakeholders. Foco em estrutura clara e breve, segurando a sala ('to hold the room').

practiceBank.title: Respostas curtas e diretas
practiceBank.how: Professor faz perguntas rápidas sobre o status; o aluno responde em no máximo duas frases, sempre direto. Cada resposta usa um alvo: 'on track', 'recommendation', 'bottom line', 'where we stand'. Penaliza-se resposta longa. Treina concisão executiva.

practiceBank.title: O que torna uma fala executiva
practiceBank.how: Apresentam-se 5 traços (ser breve, ter confiança, ir ao ponto, recomendar, segurar a sala). O aluno ordena por importância e justifica em inglês usando 'confidence', 'to get to the point', 'to come across as', 'to hold the room'. Professor desafia o ranking.

pill.tip: Depois de som sonoro ou vogal, o '-s' soa como /z/: 'deals', 'numbers', 'goes'. A garganta vibra — é um zumbido.
pill.sample: She closes deals and goes over the numbers.

lessons.title: Regional differences (NE, South, Midwest, West Coast)
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você conversará, em inglês simples, sobre as regiões dos Estados Unidos — perguntando de onde a pessoa é e descrevendo como é o lugar.
lessons.overview:
The United States is very big. It has different regions, and each one has its own style. There is the Northeast, the South, the Midwest, and the West Coast. People from each region speak and act in a different way.

This matters for Racional. Your American clients from Microsoft, Amazon, or Google can be from any of these regions. A client from New York is often fast and direct. A client from the South is often warm and laid-back. When you know this, you connect better.

You do not need to be an expert. You only need to ask good questions and show interest. "Which part of the US are you from?" or "What is it like there?" open a friendly talk. This small talk builds trust before the work talk starts.
lessons.intro:
Nesta prática você vai treinar perguntas leves para conhecer a região do cliente. Lembre destas frases-âncora: "Which part are you from?" / "What is it like there?" / "People there are very laid-back."

O objetivo aqui é conexão, não negócio. Tom leve e curioso.
lessons.situation: Antes da reunião começar, você conversa com o representante do cliente americano e descobre de qual parte dos EUA ele é.
lessons.context: So, which part of the US are you from? Oh, the West Coast, nice. What is it like there? I hear people there are very laid-back. I have never been, but I have a soft spot for that part of the country. Maybe one day I will visit.

vocab.example: New York is in the Northeast.
California is on the West Coast.
He is very down to earth.
The South is known for hospitality.

vocab.en: to have a soft spot for
vocab.example: I have a soft spot for the South.

exercises.title: 1. Ligue a região ao lugar
exercises.explanation: Saber a região ajuda você a conversar e a entender o estilo de cada cliente.

exercises.title: 2. Comece a conversa
exercises.prompt: O cliente acabou de chegar à call. Como você abre um papo leve sobre a região dele?

options.text: Which part of the US are you from?
Let me get to the point about the project.
options.whyWrong: Isso é trabalho, não conexão. O momento aqui é de small talk, antes do negócio.

options.text: Your region is not important to me.
options.whyWrong: Isso fecha a conversa e soa frio. Mostre interesse pela pessoa.

exercises.explanation: Uma pergunta simples e curiosa abre a conversa e cria conexão com o cliente.

exercises.title: 3. Pergunte em voz alta
exercises.targetText: Which part of the US are you from? What is it like there?
exercises.translation: De que parte dos EUA você é? Como é lá?
exercises.prompt: Você conversa com o cliente antes da reunião. Fale com tom leve e curioso.
exercises.explanation: Duas perguntas curtas que mostram interesse genuíno pela pessoa.

exercises.title: 4. Responda com interesse
exercises.prompt: O cliente diz que é do Sul dos EUA (the South). Escreva 2 frases curtas reagindo, usando ao menos 2 termos da aula em inglês.
keywords: soft spot|What's it like|what is it like
exercises.modelAnswer: Oh, the South, nice! I hear people there are very warm. I have a soft spot for that part of the country. What is it like there?
exercises.explanation: A correção olha só o uso dos termos. Reaja com interesse e faça uma pergunta de volta.

lessons.critical: Em voz alta, por 15 a 20 segundos, converse com o cliente americano antes da reunião. Pergunte de que parte dos EUA ele é e como é morar lá.
takeaways: I can name US regions in English.
I can ask where a client is from.
I can ask what a place is like.
I can show interest in small talk.

activities.title: Four Big Regions
activities.body:
The United States is a very big country. People often talk about four regions. The Northeast has big cities like New York and Boston. The South is warm and famous for friendly people and good food. The Midwest is in the center, with farms and quiet towns. The West Coast is by the Pacific Ocean, with cities like Los Angeles and Seattle.

Each region has its own weather, food, and way of life. When you meet an American, you can ask, "Which part are you from?" It is a nice way to start a conversation.

question.q: Qual opção resume melhor o texto?

options.text: The United States has four main regions, and each one has its own cities, weather, and way of life.
New York and Boston are the two most important cities in the United States.
The West Coast is the best region because it is near the ocean.
Americans like to talk about food when they meet new people.

activities.title: The Friendly South
activities.body:
The South is known for its warm weather and warm people. Many Southerners are very polite. They often say "please" and "thank you," and they like to talk with strangers. People call this "Southern hospitality."

The food in the South is famous too. People eat fried chicken, barbecue, and sweet tea. Music is also important here. Country music and the blues started in the South.

If an American says they are from the South, you can ask about their favorite food. Many people from the South love to share their food and culture.

question.q: Qual opção resume melhor o texto?

options.text: The South is famous for friendly, polite people, good food, and music.
Fried chicken and barbecue are the only foods people eat in the United States.
Country music and the blues are popular all over the world today.
Southerners always say "please" and "thank you" when they eat sweet tea.

activities.title: Laid-Back West Coast
activities.body:
The West Coast is by the Pacific Ocean. It has the states of California, Oregon, and Washington. People here are often called "laid-back." This means they are relaxed and easygoing.

The West Coast has many beaches, mountains, and big technology companies. Cities like Seattle and San Francisco are home to companies like Amazon and Microsoft. The weather is sunny in California and more rainy in the north.

People on the West Coast often wear casual clothes, even at work. If you meet someone from this region, you can ask about the beaches or the mountains.

question.q: Qual opção resume melhor o texto?

options.text: The West Coast is a relaxed region by the ocean, with beaches, mountains, and big technology companies.
Amazon and Microsoft are the two biggest companies in the whole world.
California always has sunny weather and many beautiful beaches.
People on the West Coast do not like to wear formal clothes anywhere.

lessons.title: Contract management overview
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você descreverá, em inglês simples, as fases do ciclo de vida de um contrato e dirá se o projeto está no prazo.
lessons.overview:
A contract has a lifecycle. It moves through phases, from the start to the end. First the client gives the award. Then there is a kickoff. Then comes the execution, the monitoring, and at the end, the closeout.

For Racional, this lifecycle can last 18 to 24 months. A data center for an American client is a long trip. As the contract manager, you must know which phase you are in and what comes next. This helps you talk to the client with a clear plan.

Each phase has a goal. In execution, you watch the scope, the timeline, and each milestone. You give the client a status report and you say if you are on track. When you speak the language of the lifecycle, the client sees you are in control.
lessons.intro:
Nesta prática você vai treinar como falar das fases do contrato. Lembre destas frases-âncora: "We are in the execution phase." / "The next milestone is in May." / "We are on track."

Saber nomear a fase atual passa controle ao cliente.
lessons.situation: O cliente americano pede um resumo de onde o contrato está. Você explica a fase atual e o próximo marco.
lessons.context: Let me give you a quick status report. We are in the execution phase now. The next milestone is the slab, in May. The scope is clear and the timeline is good. The bottom line is, we are on track for the closeout in March.

vocab.example: Contract management is my main job.
We are in a new phase.
We are in the execution phase.
The next milestone is in May.
The client is a key stakeholder.

exercises.title: 1. Qual fase é esta?
exercises.prompt: A obra está em andamento e você acompanha o avanço todos os dias. Qual fase do ciclo do contrato é esta?

options.text: the kickoff
options.whyWrong: O kickoff é a reunião de início, antes da obra começar de verdade.

options.text: the execution phase
the closeout
options.whyWrong: O closeout é o encerramento, no fim do contrato.

exercises.explanation: Execução (execution) é a fase em que a obra acontece e você monitora o avanço.

exercises.title: 2. Ligue o termo à tradução
exercises.explanation: Estes termos são a base para falar do ciclo de vida do contrato com o cliente.

exercises.title: 3. Ouça e escreva
exercises.correctText: We are in the execution phase now.
exercises.explanation: Frase direta para dizer ao cliente em qual fase do contrato a obra está.

exercises.title: 4. Escreva o status
exercises.prompt: Escreva 2 ou 3 frases dando um status curto ao cliente: diga a fase atual e o próximo marco. Use ao menos 2 termos da aula em inglês.
exercises.modelAnswer: We are in the execution phase now. The next milestone is in May. The timeline is good and we are on track.
exercises.explanation: A correção olha só o uso dos termos. Diga a fase e o próximo marco com clareza.

exercises.title: 5. Dê o status em voz alta
exercises.targetText: We are in the execution phase. The next milestone is in May, and we are on track.
exercises.translation: Estamos na fase de execução. O próximo marco é em maio, e estamos no prazo.
exercises.prompt: O cliente quer um resumo rápido. Fale com calma e segurança.
exercises.explanation: Diga a fase, o próximo marco e se está no prazo. Curto e claro.

lessons.critical: Em voz alta, por 15 a 20 segundos, dê ao cliente americano um resumo do contrato: diga a fase atual, o próximo marco e se a obra está no prazo.
takeaways: I can name the phases of a contract.
I can say which phase we are in.
I can talk about the next milestone.
I can give a short status report.
I can say if we are on track.

practiceBank.how: O aluno na cadeira quente: o diretor (professor) dispara perguntas sobre fase, marco e prazo sem aviso. O aluno responde na hora usando 'where we are', 'milestone', 'on schedule', 'status report'. Treina resposta rápida e segura sobre o contrato.

pill.tip: Há letras que não se pronunciam: o 'b' de 'debt' e 'climb', o 'p' de 'receipt', o 's' de 'island'. Diga 'det' (sem o 'b') e 'climb' soando como 'claim-b' sem o 'b', quase 'claim'.

lessons.title: Reading & interpreting contracts in English
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você lerá e explicará, em inglês simples, cláusulas básicas de um contrato — entendendo a diferença entre shall, must e may.
lessons.overview:
A contract is full of clauses. Each clause is a small part with one rule. To manage a project well, you must read these clauses and understand them. You do not need perfect English. You need to know the key words.

Three small words carry a lot of weight: shall, must, and may. Shall and must mean an obligation — you have to do it. May means it is allowed, but not required. One small word can change the cost and the timeline of a Racional project.

When a clause is not clear, you ask the client to clarify. You check the wording. You make sure both parties agree before you sign off. This protects Racional and builds a long, fair relationship with the American client.
lessons.intro:
Nesta prática você vai treinar a leitura de cláusulas. Lembre destas frases-âncora: "This clause means we shall deliver in March." / "Can you clarify this term?" / "Both parties must agree."

Atenção a shall / must / may — eles mudam a obrigação.
lessons.situation: Você lê uma cláusula do contrato com o cliente americano e pede que ele esclareça uma palavra que não está clara.
lessons.context: I read this clause, and I have a question. It says the contractor shall deliver in March. So this is an obligation for us, right? But this term here is not clear. Can you clarify the wording? I want both parties to agree before we sign off.

vocab.example: The contractor shall deliver in March.
The client may visit the site.
We sign off on the plan.

exercises.title: 1. Monte a cláusula
exercises.explanation: 'Shall' marca uma obrigação. Esta é uma estrutura típica de cláusula contratual.

exercises.title: 2. Obrigação ou permissão?
exercises.prompt: The client ___ visit the site, but does not have to.
exercises.explanation: 'May' = pode (permissão), não obrigação. 'Shall' e 'must' seriam obrigação.

commonErrors.shall: 'Shall' é obrigação; aqui a ideia é permissão, então use 'may'.

exercises.title: 3. O que significa 'shall'?
exercises.prompt: A cláusula diz: 'The contractor shall deliver in March.' O que isso quer dizer?

options.text: É uma obrigação: a Racional tem que entregar em março.
É só uma sugestão; a Racional pode entregar quando quiser.
options.whyWrong: 'Shall' não é sugestão. Em contratos, 'shall' marca obrigação.

options.text: É uma permissão: a Racional pode entregar se quiser.
options.whyWrong: Permissão é 'may'. 'Shall' é obrigação.

exercises.explanation: Em contratos, 'shall' e 'must' marcam obrigação. 'May' marca permissão.

exercises.title: 4. Ligue o termo à tradução
exercises.explanation: Estes termos ajudam você a ler e discutir cláusulas com o cliente.

exercises.title: 5. Peça um esclarecimento
exercises.prompt: Uma cláusula não está clara. Escreva 2 frases pedindo ao cliente para esclarecer a redação antes de assinar. Use ao menos 2 termos da aula em inglês.
exercises.modelAnswer: This clause is not clear to me. Can you clarify the wording? I want both parties to agree before we sign off.
exercises.explanation: A correção olha só o uso dos termos. Pedir clareza antes de assinar protege a obra.

exercises.title: 6. Peça em voz alta
exercises.targetText: This term is not clear. Can you clarify the wording before we sign off?
exercises.translation: Este termo não está claro. Você pode esclarecer a redação antes de assinarmos?
exercises.prompt: Você lê uma cláusula com o cliente. Peça o esclarecimento de forma educada e firme.
exercises.explanation: Pedir para esclarecer não é fraqueza. É cuidado profissional com o contrato.

lessons.critical: Em voz alta, por 15 a 20 segundos, leia uma cláusula com o cliente americano, diga que um termo não está claro e peça que ele esclareça a redação antes de assinar.
takeaways: I can read a contract clause in English.
I can tell shall and must from may.
I can ask the client to clarify a term.
I can talk about an obligation.
I can ask both parties to agree before we sign off.

practiceBank.title: Pedindo para esclarecer uma cláusula

practiceBank.title: Shall, must, may na prática

practiceBank.title: É obrigação, proibição ou permissão?
practiceBank.how: Professor lê trechos de cláusula com 'shall/must/may'; o aluno classifica e explica oralmente ('This is an obligation'). Troca rápida usando 'obligation', 'to comply with', 'party', 'liability'. Treina interpretação ágil do texto contratual.

practiceBank.title: Cláusula com lacunas

practiceBank.title: Wording ambíguo no contrato

practiceBank.title: 'Shall' está ultrapassado?

practiceBank.title: Explique uma cláusula em 60s

practiceBank.title: Modais trocados

practiceBank.title: Cliente pergunta o que a cláusula significa

practiceBank.title: Reconstruindo a cláusula

lessons.title: Scope management
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você falará, em inglês simples, sobre gestão de escopo — dizendo o que está dentro ou fora do escopo e como tratar trabalho extra.
lessons.overview:
Scope is the list of work in the contract. It says what Racional will do, and what it will not do. To manage a long project well, you must know what is in scope and what is out of scope.

One big risk is scope creep. This is when small extra work is added little by little, with no new cost or time. On a 24-month data center for an American client, scope creep can hurt the budget a lot. So you must track every change.

The fix is simple and fair. When the client asks for extra work, you say it is out of scope. You explain the additional cost and the impact on the timeline. You send a quote. This is not saying no to the client. It is protecting the project and being clear with both sides.
lessons.intro:
Nesta prática você vai treinar como tratar pedidos de trabalho extra. Lembre destas frases-âncora: "That is out of scope." / "This is extra work, with an additional cost." / "I will send you a quote."

Dizer 'out of scope' com clareza protege o projeto, sem brigar com o cliente.
lessons.situation: O cliente americano pede um trabalho a mais que não estava no contrato. Você explica que é fora do escopo e que terá custo adicional.
lessons.context: I understand your request, but I need to be clear. That is out of scope. It is extra work, and it has an additional cost. I will send you a quote today. If you agree, we will add it to the contract and update the timeline.

vocab.example: The scope is in the contract.
That request is out of scope.
I will send you a quote.

exercises.title: 1. Ouça e escreva
exercises.correctText: That is out of scope.
exercises.explanation: Frase-chave para dizer, com clareza e calma, que um pedido está fora do contrato.

exercises.title: 2. Pedido fora do escopo
exercises.prompt: O cliente pede um trabalho que não estava no contrato. Qual é a melhor resposta?

options.text: No problem, we will do it for free, no need to talk.
options.whyWrong: Aceitar trabalho extra sem custo é scope creep. Isso machuca o orçamento da obra.

options.text: That is out of scope. It is extra work, with an additional cost.
No. We will not do that. It is not our problem.
options.whyWrong: Recusar de forma seca prejudica a relação. Ofereça um caminho: explique o custo e mande um quote.

exercises.explanation: Diga que é fora do escopo, explique o custo e ofereça um quote. Claro e justo, sem brigar.

exercises.title: 3. Ligue o termo à tradução
exercises.explanation: Estes termos ajudam você a tratar pedidos extras de forma profissional.

exercises.title: 4. Responda ao pedido extra
exercises.prompt: O cliente pede um trabalho a mais. Escreva 2 ou 3 frases explicando que é fora do escopo, com custo adicional, e que você vai mandar um orçamento. Use ao menos 2 termos da aula em inglês.
exercises.modelAnswer: I understand your request, but that is out of scope. It is extra work, with an additional cost. I will send you a quote today.
exercises.explanation: A correção olha só o uso dos termos. Seja claro sobre custo e ofereça um quote.

exercises.title: 5. Responda em voz alta
exercises.targetText: That is out of scope. It is extra work, with an additional cost. I will send you a quote.
exercises.translation: Isso está fora do escopo. É trabalho extra, com custo adicional. Vou te enviar um orçamento.
exercises.prompt: O cliente pediu algo a mais. Responda com firmeza e educação, sem brigar.
exercises.explanation: Tom calmo e claro. Dizer 'out of scope' protege a obra e mantém a boa relação.

lessons.critical: Em voz alta, por 15 a 20 segundos, responda ao cliente americano que pediu um trabalho extra. Diga que é fora do escopo, que tem custo adicional e que você enviará um orçamento.
takeaways: I can say what is in scope and out of scope.
I can explain that something is extra work.
I can talk about an additional cost.
I can offer to send a quote.
I can protect the project from scope creep.

practiceBank.title: Respondendo ao pedido extra

pill.tip: As letras 'ough' mudam de som: 'through' rima com 'true', 'though' rima com 'go', e 'thought' rima com 'bought'. A grafia engana — ouça cada uma.

activities.intro: Fernando, imagine que você está em uma reunião com o cliente norte-americano do Hospital. Você precisa explicar, em inglês simples, o que está dentro e fora do escopo do contrato. Monte um pitch curto seguindo os passos abaixo.

frame.label: Apresente-se e diga sua função
frame.hint: Hi, I am Fernando. I am the Contract Manager at Racional Engenharia.

frame.label: Diga qual projeto você gerencia
frame.hint: I manage the Hospital project for our US client.

frame.label: Explique o que está no escopo
frame.hint: The new operating rooms are in scope. This work is in the contract.

frame.label: Explique o que está fora do escopo
frame.hint: The parking area is out of scope. It is not in this contract.

frame.label: Fale sobre trabalho extra
frame.hint: If the client wants extra work, we make a new request and define the requirements.

frame.label: Feche com um próximo passo
frame.hint: I will send you a clear scope document this week.

activities.model: Hi, I am Fernando, the Contract Manager at Racional Engenharia. I manage the Hospital project for our US client. The new operating rooms are in scope, so this work is in the contract. The parking area is out of scope and is not in this contract. If you need extra work, we define the requirements and make a new request. I will send you a clear scope document this week.

wrapUp.prompt: Agora faça o pitch para o professor, sem ler. Diga o que está in scope e o que está out of scope no projeto do Hospital.
wrapUp.model: I am Fernando from Racional Engenharia. For the Hospital project, the operating rooms are in scope. The parking area is out of scope. For extra work, we make a new request.
wrapUp.teacherNote: Verifique se Fernando usa 'in scope' e 'out of scope' com naturalidade. Corrija a pronúncia de 'scope' (escope, não 'escopi').

activities.intro: Fernando, você vai simular uma mini-reunião com o cliente do Data Center. O cliente pede um trabalho novo, e você precisa dizer se está dentro ou fora do escopo. Use as funções abaixo.

functions.label: acompanhar (mostrar que está ouvindo)
phrases: Okay, I understand.
Yes, please continue.

functions.label: pedir esclarecimento
phrases: Sorry, can you repeat the request?
Is this part of the Data Center scope?

functions.label: confirmar
phrases: Yes, the cooling system is in scope.
Okay, this is in the contract.

functions.label: opinar
phrases: I think this new request is out of scope.
For me, this is extra work.

functions.label: interagir / propor próximo passo
phrases: Let's define the requirements together.
I will send you a new scope document.

activities.task: Simule uma reunião de 4-5 minutos: o professor (cliente) pede uma sala extra no Data Center. Fernando ouve, pede esclarecimento, confirma o que está in scope, diz que a sala extra é out of scope e propõe tratar como extra work com um novo request.

wrapUp.prompt: Conte ao professor como foi a reunião: o que o cliente pediu e o que você respondeu sobre o escopo.
wrapUp.model: The client asked for an extra room in the Data Center. I said the cooling system is in scope. The extra room is out of scope, so it is extra work. We will define the requirements and make a new request.
wrapUp.teacherNote: Foque no uso de 'request', 'extra work' e 'to define'. Ajude Fernando a separar 'in scope' (já no contrato) de 'extra work' (pedido novo).

image.alt: A team in a business meeting talking around a table.

activities.instruction: Fernando, olhe a foto desta reunião. Imagine que é uma reunião sua na Racional sobre o escopo do projeto do Hospital. Responda às perguntas em inglês simples.
questions: How many people are in the meeting?
Where are the people?
What are they talking about?

wrapUp.model: This is a meeting at Racional Engenharia. The people talk about the Hospital project. They define the scope: some work is in scope and some is out of scope. I am the Contract Manager, and I take notes about the requirements.
wrapUp.teacherNote: Incentive frases simples com 'there is / there are'. Reforce o vocabulário 'scope', 'requirement' e 'request' na descrição.

lessons.title: Change orders 1: requesting & justifying
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você vai saber pedir uma change order (mudança de escopo) e justificar o motivo dela em inglês simples, com o cliente.
lessons.overview:
A change order is a formal request to change the contract. On every big project, things change. The client wants a new wall. The soil is different. A new rule appears. When this happens, the work changes too. The change order puts this change in writing. It is a normal and important part of the job.

For a contract manager at Racional, change orders are part of every week. A data center for Microsoft or Amazon is large and complex. The client often asks for new things. You must explain the impact on time and cost. You must give a clear reason. A good change order protects the project and keeps trust with the client.

In this lesson you will learn to request a change and justify it. You will use short, clear sentences. You will say what changed, why it changed, and what it means for the job. This skill helps you talk with North American clients in a calm and professional way.
lessons.intro:
Vamos treinar duas estruturas-âncora simples. Para pedir: "We need to request a change order." Para justificar: "The reason is the soil condition." / "This will impact the cost and the schedule."

Lembre: o cliente quer clareza. Diga o que mudou, por que mudou e o impacto — sempre em frases curtas.
lessons.situation: Você está numa obra de data center para um cliente americano. O solo é diferente do esperado e a fundação precisa mudar. Você precisa pedir uma change order.
lessons.context: We have a problem on site. The soil is not like the plan. We need to revise the foundation. So, we need to request a change order. The reason is the soil condition. This is unforeseen. It was not in the first plan. This change will add cost and time. I will send the change order in writing today. We can talk about the impact tomorrow. Please tell me when we can proceed.

vocab.example: We need a change order for this.
I want to request a change.
I will justify the new cost.
The reason is the soil condition.
This has an impact on the cost.
The client will approve the change.
The soil condition is bad here.

exercises.title: 1. Associe o termo em inglês ao significado
exercises.explanation: Estes são os termos centrais para pedir e justificar uma change order.

exercises.title: 2. Escolha a frase correta para pedir uma change order
exercises.prompt: Você quer pedir formalmente uma mudança de escopo. O que diz?

options.text: We need to request a change order.
We need to delete the contract.
options.whyWrong: "Delete the contract" não faz sentido aqui; você quer pedir uma mudança, não apagar o contrato.

options.text: We need to forget the plan.
options.whyWrong: "Forget the plan" não é um pedido formal de mudança de escopo.

exercises.title: 3. Complete a frase
exercises.prompt: The ___ for the change is the soil condition.
exercises.explanation: "Reason" é o motivo da mudança. The reason for the change is the soil condition.

exercises.title: 4. Escreva o pedido
exercises.prompt: Escreva 2 frases curtas pedindo uma change order. Use ao menos 2 termos da aula (por exemplo: change order, reason, impact, in writing).
exercises.modelAnswer: We need to request a change order. The reason is the soil condition, and it will impact the cost.
exercises.explanation: A correção é só sobre o uso dos termos da aula. Frases curtas são ótimas.

exercises.title: 5. Leia em voz alta
exercises.targetText: We need to request a change order because of the soil condition.
exercises.translation: Precisamos solicitar uma ordem de mudança por causa da condição do solo.
exercises.prompt: Você está numa reunião com o cliente americano. Leia a frase com calma e clareza.
exercises.explanation: Foque em "change order" e "soil condition". Fale devagar.

lessons.critical: Em voz alta, por 15-20 segundos, peça uma change order ao seu cliente: diga o que mudou, o motivo (soil condition / unforeseen) e o impacto no custo e no prazo.
takeaways: I can request a change order in English.
I can give a clear reason for a change.
I can say a change will impact cost and time.
I can ask the client to proceed.

practiceBank.title: Respondendo ao cliente por voz

practiceBank.title: Cadeira quente do change order

practiceBank.how: O aluno fala um minuto sem parar sobre como e por que pedir uma change order em obra de data center. Deve encaixar 'to request', 'to justify', 'reason', 'impact' e 'unforeseen'. O professor cronometra e marca os termos usados.

practiceBank.title: Frase pronta para o cliente

pill.tip: Em 'tough' e 'enough' o 'ough' soa como '-uf' (rima com 'stuff'); em 'cough' soa como '-óf'. Aqui o 'gh' vira som de 'f'.

lessons.title: Music talk 1: Seal — favorite artist & live shows
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você vai saber falar do seu artista favorito (Seal) e de shows ao vivo, para criar conexão com o cliente.
lessons.overview:
Music is a great way to connect with people. Before and after a meeting, you can talk about small things. You can talk about food, travel, family, or music. Music is easy and warm. It helps you build a real friendship with your client.

You love Seal. He is a British soul singer. His voice is strong and special. When you talk about a favorite artist, you show your human side. North American clients enjoy this. A long project at Racional can take 18 to 24 months. In that time, small talk builds trust.

In this lesson you will learn simple words about music and live shows. You will say you are a huge fan. You will talk about a gig you saw. This is light and fun English, but it has a clear goal: to make a strong bond with your client.
lessons.intro:
Vamos treinar frases-âncora para falar de música. Para gosto: "I am a huge fan of Seal." / "I am really into soul music." Para shows: "I saw him live last year. The crowd was amazing."

Tom leve e conversacional — é small talk, não reunião formal.
lessons.situation: Antes da reunião, o cliente americano comenta que gosta de música. Você aproveita para falar do Seal e de um show que viu.
lessons.context: I love music. I am a huge fan of Seal. He sings soul music. His voice is amazing and unmistakable. I saw him live two years ago. The show was great. The crowd was big. We all sang along. I had goosebumps. His songs are the soundtrack of my life. Do you like soul music too?

vocab.example: I am really into soul music.
I am a huge fan of Seal.
I saw him live last year.
I had goosebumps at the show.
I love the lyrics of this song.
His songs are the soundtrack of my life.

exercises.title: 1. Associe o termo em inglês ao significado
exercises.explanation: Palavras simples para falar de música e shows.

exercises.title: 2. Escolha a frase correta
exercises.prompt: Você quer dizer que gosta muito de Seal. O que diz?

options.text: I am a huge fan of Seal.
I am a small wall of Seal.
options.whyWrong: "Small wall" não tem sentido aqui; o correto é "huge fan" (grande fã).

options.text: I am afraid of Seal.
options.whyWrong: "Afraid of" significa ter medo, não gostar.

exercises.title: 3. Leia em voz alta
exercises.targetText: I am a huge fan of Seal. I saw him live last year.
exercises.translation: Eu sou um grande fã do Seal. Eu o vi ao vivo no ano passado.
exercises.prompt: Conversa leve antes da reunião. Leia com um sorriso na voz.

activities.title: Who Is Seal?
activities.body:
Seal is a British singer. He was born in London in 1963. He sings soul and pop music. His voice is warm and strong. Many people say his voice is unmistakable. You hear one note, and you know it is Seal.

His most famous song is "Kiss from a Rose." It came out in 1994. The song won big music prizes. Today, people still love it. If you are a huge fan of soul music, Seal is a great artist to talk about with friends or clients.

question.q: Qual opção resume melhor o texto?

options.text: Seal is a British soul and pop singer with a famous, unmistakable voice and a hit song called "Kiss from a Rose."
Seal is a British singer who was born in London in 1963.
"Kiss from a Rose" is a song from 1994 that won many prizes.
British music is very popular all around the world today.

activities.title: Going to a Live Show
activities.body:
A live show is special. People call it a concert or a gig. You buy a ticket, and you go to see your favorite artist live.

At the show, there is a big crowd. People sing together. They clap their hands and dance. The music is loud, and the energy is strong. You can feel it in your body.

To see someone live is different from listening at home. At home, the song is small. At a live show, the song is big and real. Many fans say it is the best way to enjoy music.

question.q: Qual opção resume melhor o texto?

options.text: Seeing an artist live at a concert, with a big crowd and strong energy, is special and different from listening at home.
At a live show, you need to buy a ticket before you can go in.
People dance and clap their hands when they hear loud music.
Listening to music at home is small, quiet, and not very fun.

activities.title: Talking About Music
activities.body:
Music is a warm and easy topic. Before or after a meeting, you can talk about small things. Music is a great choice because everybody likes some kind of music.

You can ask simple questions. "What music are you into?" or "Who is your favorite artist?" People love to talk about the songs they enjoy.

You can also share your story. You can say, "I am a huge fan of Seal," or "I saw him live last year." These small talks help you build a real friendship with a client. Music brings people together.

question.q: Qual opção resume melhor o texto?

options.text: Music is an easy, warm small-talk topic that helps you connect with a client through simple questions and personal stories.
You should ask a client "What music are you into?" before every meeting.
Everybody in the world likes at least one kind of music.
Small talk is the best way to start any business meeting.

lessons.title: Change orders 2: negotiating cost & time impact
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você vai saber negociar o impacto de custo e prazo de uma change order em inglês simples.
lessons.overview:
A change order has a price and a time. When the work changes, the cost changes and the schedule changes too. The client wants to know: how much more, and how many more days. This is the cost impact and the time impact. You must explain both in a clear way.

At Racional, you talk about these numbers every week. A change on a data center can add cost and push the deadline. The client may want a lower price or a faster job. So you negotiate. You break down the numbers. You show labor and material. You look for a fair trade-off that works for both sides.

In this lesson you will learn to discuss money and time in a calm way. You will use short sentences to ask for more time and more cost. You will learn to agree on a number in writing. This keeps the relationship with your North American client strong and clear.
lessons.intro:
Frases-âncora desta aula: "This change has a cost impact and a time impact." / "We need to push the deadline by two weeks." / "Let me break down the numbers for you."

Negociar é dar e receber: "We can do this, but we need a time extension."
lessons.situation: O cliente aprovou a mudança de fundação, mas quer entender o custo extra e o novo prazo. Você negocia o impacto.
lessons.context: Let me break down the numbers. This change has a cost impact. The labor will add more cost. There is also a time impact. We need to push the deadline by two weeks. We can proceed, but we need a time extension. I think this is a fair trade-off. Can we agree on this? I will put the new cost and date in writing.

vocab.example: There is a time impact too.
We need a small cost adjustment.
We need to push back the deadline.
Let me break down the numbers.
Can we agree on this price?
I will send it in writing.

takeaways: I can explain the cost impact of a change.
I can ask for a time extension.
I can break down the numbers for the client.
I can agree on a price in writing.

lessons.title: Claims management
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você vai saber abrir um claim (pleito), explicar o motivo e apoiar com evidências em inglês simples.
lessons.overview:
A claim is a formal request for time or money. Sometimes a problem is not your fault. The client is late with a drawing. The weather stops the work. A new rule appears. These things are out of our control. When this happens, you may be entitled to more time or more cost. You raise a claim.

For a contract manager at Racional, a good claim is built on facts. You need evidence. You need records: photos, emails, and reports. On a long project for Amazon or Google, small delays add up. Clear records protect the company. They show the problem was real and not your fault.

In this lesson you will learn to file a claim in a fair and calm way. You will say what happened, why it was out of your control, and how you can support it. This is a key skill to defend the project and keep a fair relationship with your client.
lessons.intro:
Frases-âncora: "We need to raise a claim." / "This delay was out of our control." / "We have records to support the claim."

Um bom claim é calmo e baseado em fatos, nunca em emoção.
lessons.situation: O cliente atrasou a entrega de um projeto e isso parou uma frente de serviço. Você precisa abrir um claim para pedir mais prazo.
lessons.context: We have a problem. The new drawing was late. This delay was out of our control. It stopped one work front. We could not start the job. So, we need to raise a claim. We are entitled to more time. We have records to support the claim. I have photos and emails. We only want a fair result. Let me file the claim today.

vocab.example: We need to raise a claim.
We are entitled to more time.
The delay was caused by the client.
This was out of our control.
I will file the claim today.

exercises.modelAnswer: We need to raise a claim because the delay was out of our control. We have records to support it.
exercises.explanation: A correção é só sobre o uso dos termos. Mantenha o tom calmo e factual.

takeaways: I can raise a claim in English.
I can say a delay was out of our control.
I can support a claim with records.
I can ask for fair compensation.

lessons.title: Pricing discussions in operations
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você vai saber discutir e justificar preços na operação, em inglês simples, com o cliente.
lessons.overview:
Money is part of every project. During the work, you talk about price many times. The client asks about a figure. You explain why the number is fair. You show what is in the scope of work. Sometimes the client wants a discount. You must hold a clear and calm line.

At Racional, pricing talks happen with care. A large client like Microsoft wants value for money. You want a fair margin. Both sides need to win. So you explain your numbers. You show why the price reflects the work. When needed, you find a way to meet halfway.

In this lesson you will learn to talk about prices in a simple way. You will justify a figure, answer a concern, and offer something in exchange for a lower price. This helps you protect the margin and keep a good, fair relationship with your North American client.
lessons.intro:
Frases-âncora: "This price reflects the full scope of work." / "I understand your concern." / "We can lower the price, but in exchange for a smaller scope."

O objetivo é justificar o preço sem perder o cliente.
lessons.situation: O cliente acha o preço alto e pede desconto. Você precisa justificar a cifra e, se possível, propor uma troca justa.
lessons.context: I understand your concern about the price. Let me explain the figure. This price reflects the full scope of work. It is a fair number. We give you good value for money. I cannot lower the price for free. But we can meet halfway. We can reduce the cost in exchange for a smaller scope. Is this fair for you?

lessons.title: Contract types: cost-plus, lump-sum & GMP
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você vai saber explicar os tipos de contrato (cost-plus, lump-sum e GMP) e quem assume o risco, em inglês simples.
lessons.overview:
A project can use different contract types. The most common are lump-sum, cost-plus, and GMP (guaranteed maximum price). Each one shares the risk in a different way. In a lump-sum, you give a fixed price. In a cost-plus, the client pays the actual cost plus a fee. In a GMP, there is a cap on the price.

For a contract manager at Racional, the contract type changes everything. A complex data center for Microsoft may use a GMP to give the client a safe limit. A clear job with a fixed scope may use a lump-sum. You must know who carries the risk in each one. This guides how you manage cost and change.

In this lesson you will learn to name and explain each contract type in a simple way. You will say which one is predictable, which one needs trust, and which one has a cap. This helps you talk with confidence to your North American client about how the deal works.
lessons.intro:
Frases-âncora: "A lump-sum is a fixed price." / "In a cost-plus, the client pays the actual cost plus a fee." / "A GMP has a price cap."

O foco é dizer quem carrega o risco em cada modelo.
lessons.situation: O cliente americano pergunta qual tipo de contrato é melhor para a obra. Você explica as três opções de forma simples.
lessons.context: There are three main contract types. A lump-sum is a fixed price. It is simple and predictable. We carry the risk. A cost-plus is different. The client pays the actual cost plus a fee. The client carries more risk. A GMP has a price cap. It is a safe limit for the client. Each type suits a different project. Which one do you prefer?

lessons.title: American politics: parties, elections, Congress
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você entende o básico da política dos Estados Unidos — partidos, eleições e o Congresso — para acompanhar uma conversa leve com o cliente norte-americano sem se perder.
lessons.overview:
Many American clients like to talk about politics. They follow the news every day. When you work with clients from Microsoft, Amazon, or Google, they may speak about elections or about Congress. You do not need to be an expert. You only need to follow the conversation and stay polite.

The United States has two big political parties. They are the Democrats and the Republicans. People vote for a president every four years. They also vote for Congress. Congress has two parts: the Senate and the House of Representatives. These people make the laws.

On a Racional project, you will work with the same client for many months. Small talk builds trust. But politics can be a hard topic. It is smart to stay neutral. You can listen, ask a simple question, and say "What do you think?" This shows respect and keeps the relationship strong.
lessons.intro:
Nesta aula você vai praticar palavras simples sobre política dos EUA. Frases-âncora: "There are two main parties.", "People vote in November." e a pergunta segura "What do you think?".

Lembre: o objetivo é acompanhar a conversa e manter o tom neutro, nunca defender um lado.
lessons.situation: Você está num jantar com o representante do cliente americano. Ele comenta sobre as eleições e pergunta sua opinião. Você quer acompanhar e responder com elegância.
lessons.context: In the United States, there are two main parties. They are the Democrats and the Republicans. People vote for a president every four years. They also vote for Congress. Congress has two parts: the Senate and the House. Many Americans follow the news every day. Some like to talk about politics at dinner. It is fine to listen. You can stay neutral. You can ask: "What do you think?" This is a safe and polite answer.

activities.title: Two Big Parties
activities.body:
In the United States, there are two big political parties. They are the Democrats and the Republicans. Most American leaders come from one of these two parties.

The two parties do not agree on everything. They have different ideas about taxes, health, and schools. People often say the Democrats are on the "left" and the Republicans are on the "right."

Small parties also exist, but they are not strong. When Americans vote, they almost always choose a Democrat or a Republican. This is why people call it a "two-party" country.

question.q: Qual opção resume melhor o texto?

options.text: The United States has two main parties, the Democrats and the Republicans, with different ideas.
The Democrats want lower taxes for all American schools.
Many small parties win most elections in the United States.
All countries in the world have only two political parties.

activities.title: Election Day
activities.body:
Americans vote for their leaders in elections. Every four years, they vote for the President. This is the most important election in the country.

Election Day is always on a Tuesday in November. On that day, people go to a special place to vote. Today, many people also vote early or by mail.

There are also "midterm elections" in the middle of a President's four years. In these elections, people do not choose a President. They choose other leaders, like members of Congress.

question.q: Qual opção resume melhor o texto?

options.text: Americans vote in elections, including the presidential vote every four years and the midterms in between.
Americans can only vote by mail on a Tuesday in November.
The President is chosen by Congress every four years.
Election Day is a national holiday with parties and music.

activities.title: What Is Congress?
activities.body:
Congress is the part of the government that makes laws. It is in the capital city, Washington, D.C.

Congress has two parts. The first part is the Senate. Each state sends two people to the Senate, so there are one hundred senators. The second part is the House of Representatives. Bigger states send more people to the House.

The President can suggest new laws, but Congress must vote on them. So Congress and the President work together. This balance is a big idea in American politics.

question.q: Qual opção resume melhor o texto?

options.text: Congress makes the laws and has two parts, the Senate and the House of Representatives.
Congress is one group of one hundred senators in every American state.
The President alone makes all the laws in Washington, D.C.
Washington, D.C. is the biggest state and sends the most leaders.

lessons.title: Client relationship at the operational level
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você cuida do relacionamento com o cliente no nível operacional — alinhando expectativas, dando notícias com transparência e construindo confiança no dia a dia da obra.
lessons.overview:
On a long Racional project, you talk to the client every week. The project can take 18 to 24 months. In that time, you build a relationship. A good relationship is built on trust. Trust comes from clear and honest words, day after day.

The most important rule is simple: no surprises. American clients like this. If there is a small delay, tell them early. Give them a heads-up. Be transparent. When you share a problem soon, the client can help and plan. When you hide it, you lose trust.

You also need to align expectations. You and the client must be on the same page. You explain the plan, you keep them posted, and you follow up. On a data center or a hospital project, this daily care is what makes a client come back to Racional for the next job.
lessons.intro:
Nesta aula você pratica como cuidar do cliente no operacional. Frases-âncora: "I want to give you a heads-up.", "I will keep you posted." e "We are on the same page."

Lembre: notícia ruim dada cedo constrói confiança; notícia escondida destrói confiança.
lessons.situation: Houve um pequeno atraso de uma entrega de fornecedor na obra. Você precisa avisar o representante do cliente americano de forma transparente e tranquilizá-lo.
lessons.context: I want to give you a heads-up. We have a small delay. One supplier is two days late. But we are working on it. We will recover the time next week. I will keep you posted every day. There are no surprises here. I want to be straight with you. We are on the same page. Thank you for your trust.

I will be straight with you.
I will keep you posted every day.
The rain set us back two days.
We will recover the time next week.
The job is back on track now.
I want to be transparent with you.
We are on the same page.

exercises.explanation: Frase-chave para mostrar que você vai manter o cliente informado.

options.whyWrong: É vago e não é transparente.

exercises.prompt: Pratique dar uma notícia com transparência e tranquilizar o cliente.
exercises.explanation: Tom calmo e firme. Mostra controle da situação.

lessons.critical: Em voz alta, por 15-20 segundos, avise o cliente sobre um pequeno atraso na obra: dê o heads-up, diga que você vai recuperar o tempo, prometa mantê-lo informado e tranquilize-o.
takeaways: I can give the client a heads-up early.
I can be transparent and honest about delays.
I can say I will keep the client posted.
I can build trust with simple, clear words.
I can own a problem and reassure the client.

lessons.title: Owner's representative interactions
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você interage com o owner's representative (o representante do dono da obra) — entendendo o papel dele, respondendo a pedidos de informação e conduzindo inspeções e aprovações.
lessons.overview:
On every big project, the client has an owner's representative. This person works on behalf of the owner. On a Microsoft or Amazon data center, this is your main point of contact. You will see this person many times each week, on the site and in meetings.

The owner's representative has authority. This person can inspect the work and can sign off on a task. They often walk the site with you. They check if the work meets the spec. They also request information from your team. Your job is to answer clearly and on time.

A good relationship with this person is very important for Racional. You walk them through the work, you respect their questions, and you comply with their requests. When you need a decision, you may escalate it. This daily contact keeps the project moving and keeps the client happy.
lessons.intro:
Nesta aula você pratica como falar com o representante do cliente. Frases-âncora: "Let me walk you through it.", "We meet the spec." e "You are my main point of contact."

Lembre: ele tem autoridade para inspecionar e aprovar — responda com clareza e no prazo.
lessons.situation: O owner's representative do cliente americano chega à obra para uma inspeção e pede informações sobre uma etapa. Você precisa recebê-lo, mostrar o serviço e responder.
lessons.context: Good morning. You are my main point of contact here. Let me walk you through the work. This area is ready. It meets the spec. Please inspect it. If it is good, you can sign off on it. Do you need any information? I can send it today. We comply with all your requests. Thank you for coming to the site.

lessons.title: Project hand-off: from sales to delivery
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você conduz a transição de um projeto da fase de vendas para a equipe de obra (project hand-off) — recebendo escopo, cronograma e premissas do cliente.
lessons.overview:
A project does not start on the site. First, the sales team talks to the client and signs the contract. Then comes the hand-off. The sales team gives the project to the delivery team. You, as the contract manager, take over the project. This moment is very important.

In the hand-off, you receive the scope. You learn what is in scope and what is out of scope. You receive the timeline and the main milestones. You also learn the assumptions from the sale. A wrong assumption can cost time and money on a Racional job.

A clean hand-off saves the project. The sales team walks you through every deliverable and every open item. You write down the client's point of contact. Then you plan the kickoff with the client. On an Amazon or hospital project, this care at the start keeps the whole project on track.
lessons.intro:
Nesta aula você pratica receber um projeto da equipe de vendas. Frases-âncora: "What is in scope?", "Please walk me through the timeline." e "I will take over the project."

Lembre: confirme o escopo e as premissas antes do kickoff com o cliente.
lessons.situation: A equipe de vendas está passando para você um novo contrato de data center do cliente americano. Você precisa receber o escopo, o cronograma e as premissas com clareza.
lessons.context: Thank you for the hand-off. I will take over the project now. Please walk me through the scope. What is in scope and what is out of scope? I also need the timeline and the main milestones. Are there any open items? Who is the client's point of contact? I want to plan the kickoff next week. Let us confirm every assumption first.

vocab.example: Please walk me through the scope.
That extra work is out of scope.
The delivery team starts next week.
Who is the client's point of contact?
The first milestone is in March.
Please walk me through the plan.
I will take over the project.

options.text: Who is the best supplier in town?

exercises.prompt: Escreva 2 ou 3 perguntas curtas para fazer à equipe de vendas no hand-off. Use ao menos 2 termos da aula.
exercises.modelAnswer: Please walk me through the scope. What is the timeline? Who is the client's point of contact?
exercises.explanation: A correção é só sobre o uso dos termos. Frases curtas e diretas.

exercises.targetText: Please walk me through the scope and the timeline.

exercises.prompt: Pratique pedir as informações centrais do projeto.
exercises.explanation: Tom educado e profissional. Pausa após "scope".

I can ask what is in scope and out of scope.
I can ask for the timeline and the milestones.

lessons.title: Contractual notices & formal communications
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você redige e responde notificações contratuais formais (contractual notices) — comunicando atrasos, mudanças e impactos ao cliente de forma clara e profissional.
lessons.overview:
Sometimes a problem on the site is not small. It can change the deadline or the cost. In these cases, you must send a formal notice. A notice is an official message. It is always in writing. It protects Racional and the client.

A notice has a clear job. You notify the client about a delay or a problem. You explain the impact. You write what you request. The words must be calm and professional. A notice is not an angry email. It is a clear record of the facts under the contract.

On a long Racional project, formal communications keep both sides safe. You acknowledge the messages from the client. You answer by the deadline. You comply with the contract. When you write "without prejudice" or "we reserve rights", you protect the company. Clear, formal English is a strong tool for a contract manager.
lessons.intro:
Nesta aula você pratica notificações formais. Frases-âncora: "This is to notify you of a delay.", "We request a new deadline." e "We reserve our rights under the contract."

Lembre: tom calmo, sempre por escrito, com os fatos claros.
lessons.situation: Uma mudança pedida pelo cliente afetou o prazo de uma etapa. Você precisa enviar uma notificação formal informando o atraso e o impacto, e pedir um novo prazo.
lessons.context: Dear Sir, this is to notify you of a delay. A change in the design affected the work. The impact is five days on the schedule. We request a new deadline for this task. We will comply with the contract. We reserve our rights under the contract. Please acknowledge this notice in writing. Thank you.

vocab.example: This is to notify you of a delay.
Please be advised of this change.
The impact is on the schedule.
This is our right under the contract.

exercises.title: 1. Coloque na ordem certa
exercises.explanation: "This is to notify you of a delay" abre uma notificação formal.

exercises.title: 2. Complete a frase
