exercises.explanation: "In writing" = por escrito. Notificações pedem confirmação por escrito.

exercises.title: 3. Escolha a melhor frase
exercises.prompt: Você precisa pedir um novo prazo de forma formal. Qual frase usar?

options.text: We request a new deadline for this task.
Give us more time, please.
options.whyWrong: Soa informal demais para uma notificação.

options.text: We are very late, sorry.
options.whyWrong: Não pede nada e expõe a empresa sem necessidade.

exercises.title: 4. Ligue o termo à tradução
exercises.explanation: Termos centrais de uma notificação contratual.

exercises.title: 5. Escreva sua notificação
exercises.prompt: Escreva 2 ou 3 frases curtas de uma notificação formal sobre um atraso e seu impacto. Use ao menos 2 termos da aula.
exercises.modelAnswer: This is to notify you of a delay. The impact is five days on the schedule. We request a new deadline.
exercises.explanation: A correção é só sobre o uso dos termos. Tom calmo e formal.

exercises.title: 6. Leia em voz alta
exercises.targetText: We reserve our rights under the contract.
exercises.translation: Reservamos nossos direitos sob o contrato.
exercises.prompt: Pratique uma frase formal de proteção contratual.
exercises.explanation: Tom firme e neutro. Pausa após "rights".

lessons.critical: Em voz alta, por 15-20 segundos, dite uma notificação formal curta: notifique o cliente de um atraso, explique o impacto no prazo, peça um novo deadline e diga que vocês cumprem o contrato.
takeaways: I can notify the client of a delay in writing.
I can explain the impact in simple words.
I can request a new deadline.
I can ask the client to acknowledge a notice.
I can use formal phrases to protect the company.

lessons.title: Wine, food & restaurant English
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você conversa sobre comida, vinho e restaurantes — para criar vínculo com o cliente americano naquele jantar que antecede ou segue uma reunião de obra.
lessons.overview:
On a long project, business is not only on the site. Many decisions start at dinner. A relaxed meal with the American client builds a strong relationship. Food and wine are easy and friendly topics. You do not need hard words. You only need to be warm and curious.

At the table, you can ask for a recommendation. You can talk about the starter and the main course. You can say the food is delicious. You can ask the waiter to pair a wine with the meal. A simple "Cheers!" before the first sip makes a nice moment.

These small moments matter for Racional. A good dinner during an 18-month project helps you and the client trust each other. At the end, you can offer to pay: "It's on me." This warmth, in simple English, turns a client into a long-term partner.
lessons.intro:
Nesta aula você pratica conversa de restaurante. Frases-âncora: "What do you recommend?", "This is delicious." e "Cheers!"

Lembre: o tom é leve e caloroso; o objetivo é criar conexão, não fechar negócio.
lessons.situation: Você jantar com o representante do cliente americano na véspera de uma reunião de obra. Vocês conversam sobre o cardápio, pedem um vinho e brindam.
lessons.context: I am in the mood for a good steak. What do you recommend here? Let us start with a nice starter. For the main course, I will try the fish. Can you pair a red wine with it? A bottle of red, please. This food is delicious. Cheers! Thank you for tonight. The dinner is on me.

activities.title: Dinner Before Work
activities.body:
In the United States, many people like to talk about work over dinner. They call this a "business dinner." But the food is not the only goal. The dinner helps people relax and know each other better.

At the table, you can talk about easy things first. You can talk about the food, the city, or your family. After some minutes, people often start to talk about the project. A good dinner makes the next meeting friendly and warm.

question.q: Qual opção resume melhor o texto?

options.text: In the US, dinners help people relax, build a good relationship, and often lead to easy work talk.
Americans only eat dinner when they want to sign a contract.
The best food in the United States is served only at night.
People in the US never talk about their family during dinner.

activities.title: Red Wine or White Wine?
activities.body:
Wine is a friendly topic at the table. There are two common kinds: red wine and white wine. Many people say red wine is good with meat, like beef. White wine is often good with fish or chicken.

When wine goes well with food, we say it "pairs" with the food. You do not need to be an expert. You can simply ask the waiter, "What do you recommend?" This is a warm and polite question, and it always works.

question.q: Qual opção resume melhor o texto?

options.text: Wine is a friendly topic: red often pairs with meat, white with fish or chicken, and you can ask the waiter for help.
You must be a wine expert to order wine at any American restaurant.
Red wine is the only drink people order with dinner.
The waiter always brings white wine, even if you do not ask.

activities.title: Reading the Menu
activities.body:
A restaurant menu often has different parts. The first part is the starter, also called the appetizer. It is a small dish before the big one. Then comes the main course, the biggest dish of the meal.

When you are not sure what to choose, you can say, "I am in the mood for fish," or "I want to try something new." If the food is very good, you can smile and say, "This is delicious!" These small words make the dinner warm and friendly.

question.q: Qual opção resume melhor o texto?

options.text: A menu has starters and a main course, and simple phrases help you order and enjoy the meal warmly.
Every restaurant menu has exactly ten dishes to choose from.
The word "delicious" can only be used to talk about fish.
You should never speak while reading a restaurant menu.

lessons.title: Disputes & escalation paths
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você vai saber falar, em inglês simples, quando um problema deve subir de nível (escalar) e como propor uma solução justa para o cliente.
lessons.overview:
Every long project has disputes. A dispute is a serious disagreement about money, time, or scope. On a Racional project, you and the client do not always agree. This is normal. The important thing is how you solve the problem. A good contract manager stays calm and looks for a fair answer.

Some problems are small. You can resolve them on site, at your level. Other problems are bigger. They need a director or a higher manager. Moving a problem up to a higher level is called an escalation path. On a big data center for Microsoft or Amazon, the contract has clear steps. First the site team talks. If they cannot agree, the problem goes up.

Good contract managers do not fight every day. They raise an issue early, they listen, and they look for common ground. They try to compromise and act in good faith. This protects the schedule and the relationship with the American client over the next 18 to 24 months.
lessons.intro:
Hoje você vai praticar como dizer que um problema precisa subir de nível e como propor um acordo. Frases-âncora: "We have a disagreement about the schedule.", "Let's try to resolve this at our level first." e "I think we can find common ground."

Use frases curtas, uma ideia por frase. O objetivo é soar firme, mas justo.
lessons.situation: Em uma reunião semanal de obra, o representante do cliente americano não concorda com a sua data de entrega de uma laje. Você precisa decidir se resolve ali ou se leva o tema para o nível dos diretores.
lessons.context: We have a small disagreement about the slab date. I want to resolve this at our level first. I think we can find common ground today. If we cannot agree, we will follow the escalation path in the contract. But I prefer to settle this here, in good faith. Let's be fair and look at the facts together.

vocab.example: This is a small dispute about the date.
We have a disagreement about the cost.

vocab.pt: escalar, levar a um nível superior
vocab.example: We do not need to escalate this problem.
The contract has a clear escalation path.
Let's resolve this at our level.
We can solve this at our level.

vocab.pt: ponto em comum, base de acordo
vocab.example: I think we can find common ground.
We want to settle this today.
I want to raise an issue about access.
I think this is a fair solution.
Every stakeholder wants a good result.
We always work in good faith.
We are in a deadlock and need help.

exercises.title: 1. Associe o termo em inglês ao significado em português
exercises.explanation: Esses quatro termos formam a base da aula: o problema (dispute), a ação de subir (escalate), a meta (common ground) e o tom (good faith).

exercises.title: 2. Escolha a frase correta para resolver no seu nível
exercises.prompt: Você quer resolver o problema na própria reunião, sem chamar os diretores. O que você diz?

options.text: Let's escalate this now.
options.whyWrong: Escalate significa subir de nível, o contrário do que você quer aqui.

options.text: Let's resolve this at our level first.
We are in a deadlock.
options.whyWrong: Deadlock é impasse; aqui você ainda quer tentar resolver.

exercises.title: 3. Complete a frase
exercises.prompt: I think we can find ___ today and settle this.
exercises.explanation: "Find common ground" = encontrar um ponto em comum, uma base de acordo.

exercises.title: 4. Escreva sua resposta ao cliente
exercises.prompt: Escreva 2 frases curtas dizendo que você quer resolver a divergência de forma justa, no seu nível. Use ao menos 2 termos da aula em inglês.
exercises.modelAnswer: We have a small disagreement about the date. I want to resolve this at our level, in a fair way.
exercises.explanation: A correção olha só o uso dos termos: mostre que você sabe propor uma solução justa no próprio nível.

exercises.title: 5. Leia em voz alta
exercises.targetText: Let's resolve this at our level first. I think we can find common ground.
exercises.translation: Vamos resolver isso no nosso nível primeiro. Acho que podemos encontrar um ponto em comum.
exercises.prompt: Você está numa reunião de obra com o cliente americano. Fale com tom calmo e firme.
exercises.explanation: Frase de duas ideias curtas: primeiro a proposta, depois o otimismo. Pausa no ponto.

lessons.critical: Em voz alta, por 15 a 20 segundos, explique ao cliente que há uma divergência sobre uma data, que você prefere resolver no seu nível e que vai buscar uma solução justa em boa-fé. Use "disagreement", "resolve" e "common ground".
takeaways: I can say when we have a disagreement.
I can ask to resolve a problem at our level.
I can offer to find common ground.
I can talk about an escalation path in a simple way.

lessons.title: Liquidated damages & penalties
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você vai saber falar, em inglês simples, sobre multas por atraso, extensão de prazo e quando o atraso não é culpa sua.
lessons.overview:
Big contracts have penalties. The most common one is for delay. When the project is late, the client can ask for money for each late day. This is called liquidated damages. It is a fixed amount per day. For a Racional data center or hospital, this can be a lot of money, so the contract manager must understand it well.

But not every delay is your fault. Sometimes the delay is caused by the client, by bad weather, or by a problem nobody can control. In these cases, you may be entitled to an extension of time. This means the client gives you more days and does not apply the penalty. To get this, you must give notice fast and keep good records.

The contract manager must also know the cap. The cap is the maximum penalty the client can ask for. And the team must always try to mitigate the delay, which means do everything possible to recover the lost time. This protects Racional's money and its relationship with the American client.
lessons.intro:
Hoje você vai praticar como dizer que um atraso não é culpa da Racional e como pedir prazo extra. Frases-âncora: "This delay was caused by the client.", "We are entitled to an extension of time." e "There is a cap on the penalty."

Mantenha as frases curtas e use "because" para explicar a causa.
lessons.situation: O cliente americano avisa que vai aplicar a multa por atraso. Você precisa mostrar que parte do atraso foi causada por uma mudança de projeto enviada por ele, e pedir extensão de prazo.
lessons.context: I have a concern about the penalty. This delay was not our fault. It was caused by a late change from the client. So we are entitled to an extension of time. We also have a cap on the penalty in the contract. We will mitigate the delay and recover some days.

vocab.pt: multa por atraso (valor fixo em contrato)
vocab.example: The contract has liquidated damages for delay.
The client wants to apply a penalty.
Please do not apply the penalty yet.
We have a small delay this week.
This delay is not our fault.
The delay was caused by the rain.
We ask for an extension of time.
We are entitled to more days.
This clause gives us relief from the penalty.
The client agreed to waive the penalty.
The penalty is a fixed amount per day.
There is a cap on the penalty.
Heavy rain can be force majeure.

exercises.title: 1. Ouça e escreva a frase
exercises.correctText: This delay was not our fault.
exercises.explanation: Frase curta e direta para defender a posição da Racional sobre o atraso.

exercises.title: 2. Coloque as palavras na ordem correta
exercises.explanation: Estrutura: sujeito + are entitled to + substantivo. "We are entitled to an extension of time."

exercises.title: 3. Complete a frase
exercises.prompt: This delay was ___ by a late change from the client.
exercises.explanation: "Caused by" mostra a causa do atraso. Útil para dizer que a culpa não é sua.

exercises.title: 4. Escolha a frase que limita a multa
exercises.prompt: Você quer lembrar o cliente que a multa tem um limite máximo. O que você diz?

options.text: There is a cap on the penalty.
We will apply force majeure.
options.whyWrong: Force majeure é força maior, não o limite da multa.

options.text: The penalty is per day.
options.whyWrong: Isso diz como a multa é contada, não o limite máximo dela.

exercises.title: 5. Leia em voz alta
exercises.targetText: This delay was caused by a late change. We are entitled to an extension of time.
exercises.translation: Este atraso foi causado por uma mudança tardia. Temos direito a uma extensão de prazo.
exercises.prompt: Você está respondendo ao cliente que quer aplicar a multa. Fale com calma e segurança.
exercises.explanation: Primeiro a causa, depois o direito. Duas frases curtas, uma ideia em cada.

lessons.critical: Em voz alta, por 15 a 20 segundos, explique ao cliente que o atraso foi causado por uma mudança dele, que a Racional tem direito a extensão de prazo e que existe um limite (cap) na multa. Use "delay", "caused by", "entitled to" e "cap".
takeaways: I can say a delay was not our fault.
I can ask for an extension of time.
I can talk about a penalty and a cap.
I can say we will mitigate the delay.

lessons.title: Variation orders & extras
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você vai saber falar, em inglês simples, sobre serviços fora do escopo, pedidos de mudança e o impacto em custo e prazo.
lessons.overview:
During a long project, the client often asks for changes. A new wall, a different finish, an extra room. When the client wants something that is not in the original scope, the contract manager opens a variation order (also called a change order). This document records the extra work and its price.

This is very important for Racional. On a data center for Amazon or Google, small changes happen every week. If you do extra work without a change order, Racional pays and does not get the money back. So the rule is simple: when work is out of scope, you stop, you send a quote, and you wait for the client to approve it. Only then you proceed.

The contract manager must also explain the cost impact and the time impact of each change. Many small extras can grow the project little by little. This is called scope creep. To control it, you must formalize every change in writing.
lessons.intro:
Hoje você vai praticar como dizer que um serviço está fora do escopo e como pedir aprovação antes de começar. Frases-âncora: "This is out of scope.", "I will send you a quote." e "We need a change order before we proceed."

Use frases curtas e ligue causa e efeito com "so" e "because".

lessons.title: Insurance, bonds & guarantees vocabulary
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você vai saber falar, em inglês simples, sobre seguros, garantias contratuais (bonds) e responsabilidade no contrato.
lessons.overview:
Big projects need protection. Insurance protects the project against accidents, fire, and damage. A policy is the document that says what is covered. If something bad happens, you make a claim and the insurance company pays. Every site at Racional must be insured before work starts.

The contract also asks for bonds and guarantees. A performance bond protects the client if the contractor does not finish the work. An advance payment guarantee protects the client when money is paid early. These documents give the American client confidence to sign a contract with Racional for a data center or a hospital.

The contract manager must know what the company must provide and when. You must also understand liability (who is responsible) and the warranty (the promise to fix problems after handover). When you speak about these topics in English, simple and clear words protect Racional and build trust.
lessons.intro:
Hoje você vai praticar como falar sobre o que o contrato exige: seguro, garantias e responsabilidade. Frases-âncora: "The site is insured.", "We will provide a performance bond." e "The policy covers fire and damage."

Mantenha as frases curtas. Diga o documento + a ação (provide, cover, claim).
lessons.situation: Antes do início da obra, o cliente americano pede que você confirme os seguros e apresente a garantia de performance. Você precisa responder de forma clara e profissional.
lessons.context: The site is insured. We have a valid policy. It covers fire, accidents, and damage. If we have a problem, we make a claim. We will also provide a performance bond and an advance payment guarantee. The warranty period starts after handover.

lessons.title: US economy: Fed, inflation, interest rates
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você vai saber conversar, em inglês simples, sobre a economia dos EUA — juros, inflação e o impacto no custo da construção.
lessons.overview:
American clients talk about the economy a lot. They watch the Fed, the central bank of the United States. The Fed sets the interest rate. When prices go up too fast, this is called inflation. To fight inflation, the Fed may raise rates. When the economy is slow, it may cut rates.

Why does this matter to a contract manager? Interest rates change the cost to borrow money. When rates are high, financing a big project is more expensive. This can make an Amazon or Microsoft client delay a new data center, or push hard on price. The cost of materials like steel and concrete can also go up with inflation.

You do not need to be an economist. But when your American client talks about the Fed, inflation, or the market, you can follow the conversation and connect. A simple comment like "We keep an eye on the cost of materials" shows that you understand their world. This builds a stronger relationship.
lessons.intro:
Hoje a conversa é mais leve e cultural: economia americana como assunto de relacionamento. Frases-âncora: "The Fed may raise rates.", "Financing is more expensive now." e "We keep an eye on the cost of materials."

Use frases curtas. O objetivo é conversar, não dar uma aula de economia.
lessons.situation: Num café antes da reunião, o representante do cliente americano comenta sobre os juros altos nos EUA. Você quer participar da conversa e conectar com o custo de materiais.
lessons.context: The Fed may raise rates again this year. Inflation is still a little high. So financing a big project is more expensive now. We also see the cost of materials go up. We keep an eye on steel and concrete prices. It is good to watch the market.

pill.tip: As vogais átonas viram um 'schwa', um 'ã' fraco e neutro. Em 'banana' só a sílaba do meio é forte: 'bã-NÉ-nã'. Não pronuncie cada vogal cheia.

activities.title: What Is the Fed?
activities.body:
The Fed is the central bank of the United States. Its full name is the Federal Reserve. The Fed is very important for the American economy. It helps keep prices stable and helps people find jobs.

One big job of the Fed is to set the interest rate. The interest rate is the cost of money. When you borrow money, you pay this cost. Banks, companies, and families all watch the Fed. When the Fed talks, the whole country listens. American clients often talk about the Fed in meetings, so it is good to know what it does.

question.q: Qual opção resume melhor o texto?

options.text: The Fed is the central bank of the United States, and it sets the interest rate and helps keep the economy stable.
The Fed only helps families borrow money to buy a house.
The Fed is a private company that sells goods to other countries.
The Fed controls all the banks in the whole world.

activities.title: Inflation: When Prices Go Up
activities.body:
Inflation means prices go up over time. Last year a coffee was three dollars. This year the same coffee is four dollars. That is inflation.

A little inflation is normal and not a problem. But when prices go up too fast, life gets hard. Food, gas, and rent cost more money. Families feel worried because their money buys less.

To fight high inflation, the Fed can raise interest rates. When rates are higher, money costs more, so people spend less. Slowly, prices stop going up so fast. This is why American clients watch inflation news very closely.

question.q: Qual opção resume melhor o texto?

options.text: Inflation is when prices go up, and the Fed can raise interest rates to slow it down.
Inflation only affects the price of coffee in the United States.
Inflation is always good and helps families buy more food.
Inflation happens because the Fed cuts interest rates every year.

activities.title: Interest Rates and Building Costs
activities.body:
Interest rates touch many parts of life, even construction. Big projects, like a hospital or a data center, cost a lot of money. Often companies borrow money from a bank to pay for the work. This is called financing.

When the Fed raises rates, borrowing money costs more. So the project costs more too. When the Fed cuts rates, borrowing is cheaper, and building is cheaper.

This is why people who work in construction follow the Fed. A small change in rates can change the price of a big project. For an American client, this news is part of normal business talk.

question.q: Qual opção resume melhor o texto?

options.text: Interest rates set by the Fed change the cost of borrowing money, which affects the price of building projects.
Hospitals and data centers never need to borrow money from a bank.
The Fed builds hospitals and data centers in the United States.
Construction companies do not care about interest rates at all.

lessons.title: Project closeout & contract termination
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você vai saber falar, em inglês simples, sobre o encerramento da obra, entrega final e os tipos de rescisão de contrato.
lessons.overview:
Every project has an end. The last phase is called closeout. At closeout, the team makes a punch list. This is a list of small outstanding items to fix before the client accepts the work. When the list is done, the client gives final acceptance and you do the handover.

Closeout has important documents and money steps. You deliver the as-built drawings, which show how the building was really made. The client then releases the retention and pays the final payment. After handover, the warranty period begins. For a Racional data center or hospital, a clean closeout protects the relationship and opens the door for the next project.

The contract can also end by termination. There are two types. For cause means one side broke the contract. For convenience means the client simply decides to stop, even when there is no problem. A good contract manager knows the difference and can talk about both calmly in English with the American client.
lessons.intro:
Hoje você vai praticar o vocabulário de encerramento e entrega da obra. Frases-âncora: "We have a short punch list.", "Please sign off on the handover." e "Then you release the retention."

Frases curtas, na ordem dos passos: corrigir, aceitar, entregar, pagar.
lessons.situation: A obra está quase pronta. Na reunião final com o cliente americano, você apresenta a punch list, pede a aceitação e organiza a entrega e o pagamento final.
lessons.context: We are at closeout now. We have a short punch list with a few outstanding items. We will fix them this week. Then we ask for final acceptance and we do the handover. We will give you the as-built drawings. After that, please release the retention and the final payment.

vocab.example: We have a short punch list.
We will give you the as-built drawings.
The final payment comes after handover.
The client will release the money.
We hope there is no termination.
The client may end it for convenience.
The warranty period starts at handover.

vocab.pt: dar o aceite, assinar a aprovação

exercises.explanation: Frase de abertura do encerramento: apresentar a lista de pendências finais.

lessons.critical: Em voz alta, por 15 a 20 segundos, conduza o encerramento: diga que há uma punch list curta, peça a aceitação final e a entrega, e peça que o cliente libere a retenção e o pagamento final. Use "closeout", "punch list", "handover" e "release the retention".
takeaways: I can talk about closeout and the punch list.
I can ask for final acceptance and the handover.
I can ask the client to release the retention.
I can explain termination for cause and for convenience.

lessons.title: Lessons learned with the client
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você conduz uma reunião de lições aprendidas (lessons learned) com o cliente — destacando o que funcionou, o que pode melhorar e os próximos passos.
lessons.overview:
At the end of a project, good teams stop and look back. This meeting is called lessons learned. The team talks about what went well and what they want to improve. The goal is simple: make the next project better. American clients like this meeting a lot. It is calm, honest, and looks to the future.

For a contract manager at Racional, this meeting matters every day. Racional builds offices, hospitals, shopping centers, and big data centers for clients like Microsoft, Amazon, and Google. These clients come back for the next project. A clear lessons learned meeting shows that Racional learns and grows. It builds trust for the long term.

The tone is the key. We do not blame people. We talk about processes and the root cause of a problem. We start with the good news, then we share one area to improve, and we close with a clear next step. This way the client leaves the room with a good feeling and a plan for the future.
lessons.intro:
Esta é uma aula CORE sobre a reunião de lessons learned (lições aprendidas), no fim do projeto com o cliente americano. O objetivo não é apontar culpados, e sim melhorar a próxima obra juntos.

Relembre as frases-âncora: "What went well was...", "One area to improve is..." e "Going forward, we will...". Comece pelo positivo, aponte a melhoria, e feche com um próximo passo concreto.
lessons.situation: Reunião de lições aprendidas com o representante do cliente, após a entrega de um data center. Você conduz a conversa de forma construtiva.
lessons.context: Let me share our lessons learned. What went well was the safety record. We had zero lost-time incidents. One area to improve is the response time on approvals. Going forward, we will set a clear deadline for each action item. Thank you for your feedback.

vocab.example: Let me share our lessons learned.
What went well was the schedule.
One area to improve is response time.
Let me list the next steps.
Each action item has an owner.
Thank you for your honest feedback.
We look at the root cause, not the person.
We take ownership of that delay.
I will follow up next week.
Going forward, we will track this weekly.
The main takeaway is to align earlier.
We need to align on deadlines.

exercises.title: 1. Combine o termo com o significado
exercises.explanation: Esses termos deixam a sua fala madura e orientada à solução.

options.text: stay constructive and talk about processes
say everything was perfect
options.whyWrong: Não. Esconder os problemas tira o sentido da reunião — não há aprendizado.

exercises.explanation: Lessons learned é sobre melhorar processos, não culpar pessoas. Tom construtivo gera confiança.

next steps|action item|going forward|take ownership|follow up
exercises.modelAnswer: What went well was our safety record. One area to improve is the response time on approvals. Going forward, we will set a clear deadline for each action item.
exercises.explanation: Positivo primeiro, melhoria depois, próximo passo no fim — essa ordem deixa tudo construtivo.

exercises.title: 5. Conduza a reunião
exercises.prompt: Abra a reunião de lessons learned com um ponto positivo, um a melhorar e um próximo passo. Leia em voz alta.
exercises.targetText: Let me share our lessons learned. What went well was the safety record. One area to improve is the response time. Going forward, we will set a clear deadline.
exercises.translation: Deixa eu compartilhar as nossas lições aprendidas. O que foi bem foi o histórico de segurança. Um ponto a melhorar é o tempo de resposta. Daqui para frente, vamos definir um prazo claro.
exercises.explanation: Essa estrutura de três blocos mantém a reunião positiva e voltada para o futuro.

lessons.critical: Em voz alta, conte uma lição aprendida real de uma obra sua: o que foi bem, o que melhoraria e qual seria o próximo passo. Pode misturar inglês e português.
takeaways: I can open a lessons learned meeting with what went well.
I can point out an area to improve in a constructive way.
I can propose a next step or action item going forward.
I can keep the tone about processes, not people.

practiceBank.title: Reunião de lessons learned pós-entrega
practiceBank.how: Aluno conduz a reunião de lessons learned com o professor no papel de representante do cliente americano após a entrega de um data center. Ele abre dizendo 'what went well', aponta uma 'area to improve' e fecha com 'next steps'. Professor reage como cliente, pede um 'action item' e cobra que o aluno feche cada bloco com 'going forward'.

practiceBank.title: Three columns: went well / improve / next steps
practiceBank.how: Professor escreve três colunas no quadro (what went well, to improve, next steps). O aluno fala em voz alta preenchendo cada coluna sobre um projeto de data center, usando 'feedback', 'constructive' e 'takeaway'. O aluno deve produzir pelo menos duas frases por coluna; professor só anota e cobra que ele use 'to align' ao final.

practiceBank.title: Meu maior takeaway do projeto
practiceBank.how: Aluno grava 60 segundos resumindo o principal 'takeaway' de uma obra concluída e o que faria diferente 'going forward'. Deve encaixar 'root cause' e 'to take ownership' de algo que não saiu bem. Professor escuta, devolve uma correção de fluência e pede regravação mais enxuta.

practiceBank.title: Cliente faz follow-up das ações
practiceBank.how: Professor (cliente) dispara perguntas rápidas de follow-up: 'Who owns this action item?', 'What's the root cause?', 'What's the next step?'. Aluno responde sem pausas longas, sempre 'taking ownership' e prometendo 'to follow up'. Ritmo acelera a cada rodada; professor anota travas para feedback final.

practiceBank.title: De crítica seca para feedback construtivo
practiceBank.how: Professor diz uma crítica dura ('The schedule was a mess'). Aluno reformula oralmente em 'constructive feedback' usando 'an area to improve is...' e 'going forward we will...'. Faça 8-10 transformações; professor corrige tom e estrutura na hora.

practiceBank.title: Quem é dono de cada action item
practiceBank.how: Aluno tem metade da lista de action items e o professor a outra metade. Falando apenas em inglês, eles trocam informação para montar a lista completa: quem 'takes ownership', qual o 'next step' e quando 'to follow up'. Nada de mostrar o papel; só produção oral.

practiceBank.title: Defenda a área que precisa melhorar
practiceBank.how: Aluno na cadeira quente assume um problema do projeto (atraso no commissioning, por exemplo). Professor e/ou perguntas pressionam, e ele precisa 'take ownership', explicar 'root cause' e propor 'next steps' sem se defender de forma agressiva. Foco em manter o tom 'constructive'.

lessons.title: Construction industry overview: US vs. Brazil
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você compara a indústria da construção dos EUA e do Brasil em inglês simples — normas, materiais, mão de obra e fornecedores — para alinhar expectativas com o cliente americano.
lessons.overview:
The construction industry is not the same in every country. The rules, the materials, and the people are different. In the US, builders often use steel structure. In Brazil, we often use concrete. The building code and the fire code follow different standards. The workforce and the labor laws are different too. None of this is good or bad. It is just different.

For Racional, this is the heart of the work. American clients like Microsoft, Amazon, and Google bring habits from their home market. The contract manager must explain, in simple words, what is the same and what is different here. A good answer builds trust. The client sees that Racional knows the local market and respects the global standard.

This is called tropicalization. We take a global idea and we make it fit the Brazil context. We use a local supplier with a short lead time. We pick a cost-effective material. We always comply with the local code. The result is a building that works here, with the same quality the client expects.
lessons.intro:
Esta é uma aula CORE. O cliente americano traz expectativas do mercado dele. Saber explicar, em inglês simples, o que é igual e o que é diferente no Brasil evita ruído e mostra domínio.

Relembre as frases-âncora: "In the US, you usually...; in Brazil, we usually..." e "It is similar, but different."
lessons.situation: Visita técnica com o cliente americano. Ele pergunta por que o projeto usa concreto, e não estrutura metálica como nos EUA.
lessons.context: In the US, you usually build with steel structure. In Brazil, we often use concrete. It is local and cost-effective. It fits our labor laws and our fire code. It is similar, but different. The standard is high in both countries. Let me explain why concrete works here.

In the US, steel structure is common.

It is similar but different here.

lessons.title: Project lifecycle (design — build — handover)
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você descreve o ciclo de vida do projeto em inglês — do design à entrega — citando fases, marcos e se a obra está no prazo.
lessons.overview:
Every building follows the same path. We call it the project lifecycle. First comes the design phase, when the project is on paper. Then comes the construction phase, when the team builds. At the end comes the handover, when we give the building to the client. Each step has a name, and each step has a milestone — a key date that we must hit.

For Racional, this path is the same for every segment — offices, hospitals, shopping centers, and data centers. The construction phase has clear steps: foundations, then the structure, then MEP (mechanical, electrical, and plumbing), then the façade, then the finishes, and at the end the commissioning. The contract manager follows each phase and reports the status to the client.

American clients like Microsoft, Amazon, and Google ask one question all the time: are we on schedule? A clear answer builds trust. When you can walk through each phase in simple English and say what is planned for next month, the client feels safe. This lesson gives you the words to do that.
lessons.intro:
Esta é uma aula CORE sobre o project lifecycle (ciclo de vida do projeto). Você vai nomear as fases e dizer se a obra está no prazo.

Relembre as frases-âncora: "We are now in the structure phase.", "We are on schedule." e "Let me walk you through the next milestone."
lessons.situation: Reunião mensal de status. O cliente americano quer entender em que fase a obra está e o que vem a seguir.
lessons.context: Let me walk you through the project lifecycle. The design phase is done. We are now in the construction phase. The foundations are ready and the structure is up. MEP and the façade come next. We are on schedule. The next milestone is planned for July.

vocab.example: Let me explain the project lifecycle.

lessons.title: Music talk 2: Sade — British soul & timeless artists
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você fala sobre música com o cliente — descrevendo o estilo de uma artista como Sade — para criar conexão e rapport.
lessons.overview:
Music is a great way to connect with people. When a meeting ends, the small talk begins. People talk about food, travel, and music. A short, warm chat about a favorite artist builds rapport. It shows the human side. American clients enjoy this kind of easy conversation a lot.

This lesson is about Sade, a British singer with a smooth and soulful voice. Her music is mellow and timeless — it never gets old. People play it as background music at home or in a café. You can say her songs remind you of a special time. Words like these help you talk about music in simple English.

For a contract manager at Racional, these small moments matter. A project with a client like Microsoft, Amazon, or Google lasts 18 to 24 months. That is a long time. A warm chat about a song you both love builds a bond that helps in every meeting. Business is built on numbers, but trust is built on these human moments.
lessons.intro:
Esta é uma aula BRIDGE de relacionamento. O tom é leve. O objetivo é criar conexão pelo gosto musical.

Relembre as frases-âncora: "It's so smooth and mellow.", "It never gets old." e "It reminds me of my college years."

lessons.context: I really like Sade. Her voice is so smooth and soulful. The music is mellow and timeless. It never gets old. I play it as background music at home. It reminds me of my college years. It is one of my all-time favourites.

pill.tip: Em inglês, palavras de conteúdo (substantivos, verbos principais, adjetivos) recebem o acento forte; já artigos e preposições ficam fracos. Em 'We need the report by Friday', destaque 'need', 'report' e 'Friday' (sonando 'NIID', 'ri-PORT', 'FRAI-dei') e quase engula 'the' e 'by'.

activities.title: Who Is Sade?
activities.body:
Sade is a British singer. Her full name is Sade Adu. She was born in Nigeria and grew up in England. In the 1980s, she became famous around the world. Her band is also called Sade.

Sade sings soul music. Her voice is smooth and soft. People say her songs are mellow and good for relaxing. Many people play her music in the background at home or in a café.

Her songs are timeless. They never get old. Young people and old people enjoy them today, many years later.

question.q: Qual opção resume melhor o texto?

options.text: Sade is a famous British soul singer with a smooth voice, and her timeless songs are still loved today.
Sade was born in Nigeria and that is the most important fact about her.
All British singers make mellow music that is good for relaxing at home.
Many people like to play music in cafés and at home.

activities.title: What Is Soul Music?
activities.body:
Soul music started in the United States many years ago. It comes from gospel and blues. Soul songs are full of feeling. Singers put deep emotion in their voices.

A soulful song can make you happy or sad. The music is warm and human. People feel the singer's heart.

British soul is a special style. Singers like Sade and Adele are famous for it. The sound is often smooth and mellow. It is great background music when you want to chill out. Soul music helps people relax and feel calm after a long day.

question.q: Qual opção resume melhor o texto?

options.text: Soul music is an emotional style from the US, and British singers like Sade made their own smooth version of it.
Soul music is only about feeling sad after a long day at work.
Adele is the most important soul singer in the whole world.
Gospel and blues are two American styles that nobody listens to today.

activities.title: Talking About Music
activities.body:
Music is a great way to connect with people. After a meeting, you can have a short, friendly chat. This small talk builds rapport.

You can ask easy questions. "What music do you like?" or "Who is your favorite artist?" These questions show you care about the person.

When you talk about a singer like Sade, you can use simple words. You can say her voice is smooth, her songs are timeless, or the music has a nice vibe. A warm chat about music shows your human side and helps make a good friendship at work.

question.q: Qual opção resume melhor o texto?

options.text: Talking about music with easy questions and simple words is a friendly way to build rapport at work.
You should only talk about Sade and no other singer during small talk.
Meetings are boring, so people prefer to talk about music instead.
Asking "What music do you like?" is the only correct question to ask anyone.

lessons.title: Site selection & feasibility studies
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você fala em inglês sobre escolha de terreno e estudo de viabilidade — acessos, infraestrutura, energia, solo e riscos — com o cliente.
lessons.overview:
Before we build, we choose the place. This is called site selection. Then we study the place to see if the project can work. This is the feasibility study. We look at the access roads, the local infrastructure, the power supply, and the soil conditions. We also check the zoning rules. The goal is one answer: is this site viable or not?

For Racional, this step is critical, above all for data centers. A data center for a client like Microsoft, Amazon, or Google needs a lot of power and good network access. The team must assess each site and weigh every trade-off. A good study finds the risk early, when it is cheap to fix. A bad study finds it late, when it is very expensive.

The contract manager must explain this study to the client in clear English. The site must meet the requirements of the project. When you can say why a site is viable — strong power, good access, firm soil — the client trusts the decision. This lesson gives you the words to lead that conversation.
lessons.intro:
Esta é uma aula CORE sobre site selection (escolha do terreno) e feasibility study (estudo de viabilidade).

Relembre as frases-âncora: "We need to assess the site.", "The site is viable." e "It meets the requirements."
lessons.situation: Reunião inicial com o cliente americano sobre um possível terreno para um novo data center. Você apresenta os pontos do estudo de viabilidade.
lessons.context: Let me share the feasibility study. The site has good access and strong power supply. The soil conditions are firm. The zoning is fine. There is one risk: the location is far from the city. We need to assess this trade-off. In the end, the site is viable and meets the requirements.

vocab.example: Site selection is the first step.
The site is large and flat.
The power supply is strong here.
There is one risk to study.

exercises.title: 1. Monte a frase
exercises.explanation: "The site is viable" — o terreno é viável. A conclusão de um bom estudo.

exercises.title: 2. A conclusão do estudo
exercises.prompt: The site has strong power and good access. It ___ the requirements.
exercises.explanation: "It meets the requirements" = atende aos requisitos. Frase-chave para aprovar um terreno.

commonErrors.meet: Use "meets" (terceira pessoa): the site meets, não the site meet.

exercises.title: 3. O que o estudo de viabilidade avalia
exercises.prompt: Um feasibility study avalia, entre outros pontos:

options.text: the color of the office walls
options.whyWrong: Não. Isso é acabamento, vem muito depois e não decide a viabilidade.

options.text: access, power supply, and soil conditions
the lunch menu for the team
options.whyWrong: Não. O estudo olha o terreno e a infraestrutura, não a logística do dia a dia.

exercises.explanation: O estudo avalia acesso, energia, solo, zoneamento e riscos para dizer se o site é viável.

exercises.title: 4. Combine o termo com o significado
exercises.explanation: São os pontos centrais que você apresenta num estudo de viabilidade.

exercises.title: 5. Apresente um terreno
exercises.prompt: Em 2 ou 3 frases, apresente um terreno e diga se ele é viável. Use ao menos 2 termos em inglês desta aula. A correção olha só o uso dos termos.
exercises.modelAnswer: The site has good access and strong power supply. The soil conditions are firm. There is one risk: the location is far from the city. In the end, the site is viable and meets the requirements.
exercises.explanation: Pontos positivos, um risco e a conclusão de viabilidade: a estrutura de um bom resumo.

exercises.title: 6. Apresente o estudo
exercises.prompt: Apresente, em voz alta, os pontos de um terreno e a conclusão. Leia a frase-modelo.
exercises.targetText: The site has good access and strong power supply. The soil conditions are firm. There is one risk to assess. The site is viable.
exercises.translation: O terreno tem bom acesso e forte fornecimento de energia. As condições do solo são firmes. Há um risco a avaliar. O terreno é viável.
exercises.explanation: Pontos fortes, um risco e a conclusão: assim você conduz a decisão com clareza.

lessons.critical: Em voz alta, apresente um terreno real ou imaginário para um data center: acesso, energia, solo, um risco e a sua conclusão de viabilidade. Pode misturar inglês e português.
takeaways: I can explain a feasibility study in simple English.
I can describe a site by access, power, and soil conditions.
I can name one risk and one trade-off.
I can say if a site is viable and meets the requirements.

practiceBank.how: Aluno faz um pitch de 45s convencendo o cliente de que o 'site' é 'viable': destaca 'power supply', 'access' e 'infrastructure' e minimiza o 'risk'. Deve soar confiante e dizer que 'meets the requirements'. Professor reage como decisor.

practiceBank.title: Frase de viabilidade com o termo sorteado
practiceBank.how: Professor sorteia um termo (zoning, soil conditions, trade-off, to assess, viable...) e o aluno produz na hora uma frase realista de reunião de site selection. Encadeie todos; frases vagas refazem. Professor valida uso técnico.

practiceBank.title: Aluno como cliente exigente do site
practiceBank.how: Aluno vira o cliente americano e interroga o professor (engenheiro) sobre o 'feasibility study': 'Is the power supply enough?', 'What's the soil risk?', 'Does it meet our requirements?'. Ajuda a antecipar as dúvidas reais que ele ouvirá.

lessons.title: Geotechnical & soil investigation
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você fala em inglês sobre investigação do solo — sondagem, amostras, capacidade de carga e nível d'água — para alinhar a fundação com o cliente.
lessons.overview:
Before we design the foundations, we must know the ground. This is the soil investigation, also called a geotechnical survey. The team drills a borehole and takes a sample of the soil. Then they write a soil report. The report shows the bearing capacity — how much weight the ground can hold — and the level of the water table.

For Racional, this step is the base of every project, in every segment. A heavy data center for Microsoft, Amazon, or Google needs strong ground. If the soil is soft soil, the building can settle and crack. If the soil is firm soil or bedrock, the foundation is simple and safe. The right answer comes only from a good survey.

The contract manager must read the soil report and explain it to the client in clear English. A bad surprise in the ground is very expensive to fix later. When you know the site conditions early, you protect the schedule and the budget. This lesson gives you the words to discuss the soil with confidence.
lessons.intro:
Esta é uma aula CORE sobre soil investigation (investigação do solo) e geotechnical survey (sondagem geotécnica).

Relembre as frases-âncora: "We drill a borehole and take a sample.", "The soil report shows the bearing capacity." e "The soil is firm."
lessons.situation: Reunião técnica com o cliente americano sobre a fundação. Você apresenta os resultados da sondagem do solo.
lessons.context: Let me share the soil report. We drilled three boreholes and took samples. The soil is firm and the bearing capacity is good. The water table is low. The site conditions are safe for our foundation. There is no soft soil here.

vocab.example: We drill to take a sample.
There is no soft soil here.
The firm soil is good for us.
Soft soil can settle and crack.

exercises.title: 1. Ouça e escreva
exercises.correctText: The soil is firm and the bearing capacity is good.
exercises.explanation: Frase-resumo de uma boa sondagem: solo firme e boa capacidade de carga.

exercises.title: 2. Por que investigar o solo
exercises.prompt: Por que fazemos a soil investigation antes da fundação?

options.text: to choose the office colors
options.whyWrong: Não. Cor de acabamento não tem relação com o solo nem com a fundação.

options.text: to know the bearing capacity and the water table
to test the elevators
options.whyWrong: Não. Elevadores entram bem depois, no comissionamento, não na sondagem.

exercises.explanation: A sondagem mostra a capacidade de carga e o nível d'água — a base para projetar a fundação.

exercises.title: 3. Combine o termo com o significado
exercises.explanation: São os termos centrais que aparecem em qualquer relatório de solo.

exercises.title: 4. Resuma o relatório de solo
exercises.prompt: Em 2 ou 3 frases, resuma o resultado de uma sondagem. Use ao menos 2 termos em inglês desta aula. A correção olha só o uso dos termos.
keywords: bearing capacity|firm soil|soft soil|water table|site conditions
exercises.modelAnswer: We drilled three boreholes and took samples. The soil is firm and the bearing capacity is good. The water table is low. The site conditions are safe for our foundation.
exercises.explanation: Diga o que foi feito, o resultado do solo e a conclusão para a fundação.

exercises.title: 5. Apresente a sondagem
exercises.prompt: Apresente, em voz alta, o resultado da sondagem do solo. Leia a frase-modelo.
exercises.targetText: We drilled three boreholes and took samples. The soil is firm. The bearing capacity is good. The site conditions are safe.
exercises.translation: Perfuramos três furos de sondagem e coletamos amostras. O solo é firme. A capacidade de carga é boa. As condições do local são seguras.
exercises.explanation: O que foi feito, o resultado e a conclusão: a forma clara de apresentar a sondagem.

lessons.critical: Em voz alta, explique ao cliente por que a investigação do solo importa antes da fundação, e diga o que você quer ver num bom relatório de solo. Pode misturar inglês e português.
takeaways: I can explain why we do a soil investigation.
I can say we drill a borehole and take a sample.
I can read the bearing capacity in a soil report.
I can say if the soil is firm or soft.
I can say the site conditions are safe for the foundation.

practiceBank.title: A história da sondagem

lessons.title: Foundations (deep, shallow, special)
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você nomeia e diferencia os três grandes grupos de fundação — rasa, profunda e especial — em inglês simples, para explicar ao cliente norte-americano qual solução a obra vai usar e por quê.
lessons.overview:
Every building starts with the foundation. The foundation is the part under the ground. It takes the weight of the building. We call this weight the load. The foundation must carry the load to the soil. If the foundation is good, the building is safe and strong.

There are three big groups. A shallow foundation is near ground level. We use it on firm soil. A deep foundation goes down many meters. We use it on soft soil. Here we use piles to reach the strong rock. A special foundation is for hard cases, like a diaphragm wall in a deep basement.

At Racional, the soil is different on every site. A hospital, a shopping center, or a hyperscale data center for Microsoft or Amazon all need the right foundation. The contract manager must explain this choice in clear English. The client wants to know: firm soil or soft soil? Shallow or deep? This is the first step of a safe project.
lessons.intro:
Vamos retomar a lógica que liga solo e fundação: "We use shallow foundations on firm soil." e "For soft soil, we use deep foundations."

Lembre também da ideia central: "The foundation carries the load to the soil." (A fundação leva a carga ao solo.) Solo firme → rasa. Solo mole → profunda.
lessons.situation: Numa reunião de projeto de um hospital, o cliente norte-americano quer entender qual fundação a obra vai adotar. Você explica a escolha ligando-a sempre ao solo.
lessons.context: The foundation carries the load to the soil. The soil here is soft, so we use deep foundations. We drive piles down to the rock. Near the gate, the soil is firm. There we use shallow footings. This is safe and strong.

lessons.title: Structural systems: concrete vs. steel
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você compara estrutura de concreto e estrutura de aço em inglês simples, citando vantagens de cada uma para recomendar a melhor opção ao cliente norte-americano.
lessons.overview:
The structural system is the skeleton of the building. It holds the floors and the roof. There are two main choices. The first is a concrete structure. The second is a steel structure. Both use columns and beams. The space between two columns is the span.

Each system has good points. A steel frame is lightweight and faster to erect. So a steel building can be faster to build. A reinforced concrete structure has better fire resistance and can be more cost-effective in Brazil. This choice is a real trade-off. The contract manager must explain it well.

At Racional, this choice happens on every project. A hyperscale data center for Google may favor steel for speed. A hospital may favor concrete for fire resistance and cost. When you meet the North American client, you recommend the right system. You give clear reasons. This builds trust and a strong project.
lessons.intro:
Vamos retomar as frases para comparar e recomendar: "Steel is faster to build, but concrete is more cost-effective here."

Lembre da estrutura para recomendar: "I recommend a concrete structure for this project." e do termo-chave trade-off (escolha com prós e contras).
lessons.situation: O cliente norte-americano de um data center pergunta se a obra será em concreto ou aço. Você compara os dois e recomenda o melhor para o caso.
lessons.context: We have two options: a concrete structure or a steel structure. Steel is lightweight and faster to erect, so it is faster to build. Concrete has better fire resistance and is more cost-effective here. It is a trade-off. For this data center, I recommend steel.

lessons.title: Geopolitics: war, trade & global affairs
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você fala de notícias e temas globais com o cliente norte-americano de forma leve e neutra, mantendo a conversa profissional sem entrar em polêmica.
lessons.overview:
Sometimes the client wants to talk about the news. This is small talk. He may talk about global affairs: trade, a tariff, or the supply chain. Many North American clients follow the news every day. To connect with them, you can talk a little about these topics.

But this is a sensitive area. A conflict or a war is a complex situation. It is smart to stay neutral. You do not need to pick a side. You can listen and say a few words. A good question is: "What's your take?" This shows interest. Then you can change the subject back to the project.

For Racional, the client is often from the United States. Global news can have an impact on business: a tariff can change the price of steel; the supply chain can change the lead time of a part. You do not need strong opinions. You just need to listen, stay polite, and keep an eye on the topics that touch the project.
lessons.intro:
Esta é uma aula de relacionamento. O foco é conexão, não técnica. Retome a pergunta leve: "What's your take?" (Qual a sua opinião?).

Lembre também de como manter o tom neutro: "It's a complex situation. I try to stay neutral." e como voltar ao trabalho: "Anyway, let's go back to the project."
lessons.situation: No café antes da reunião, o cliente norte-americano comenta uma notícia de comércio internacional. Você responde de forma leve, neutra e simpática.
lessons.context: Client: Did you see the news about the new tariff? It can change steel prices. What's your take? You: It's a complex situation. I try to stay neutral. But yes, we keep an eye on it. It can have an impact on our supply chain. Anyway, let's go back to the project.

vocab.example: I follow the news every morning.
Trade between the two countries is big.
A new tariff can raise the price.
The supply chain is slow this month.

We keep an eye on the prices.

There is some uncertainty in the market.

activities.title: News as Small Talk
activities.body:
Many North American people read the news every day. They read about the world, business, and global affairs. Sometimes they want to talk about it with you.

This is small talk. You can say a little, but you do not need to know everything. You can say, "I saw that in the news," or ask, "What's your take?"

It is good to listen more than you talk. Stay calm and friendly. The goal is to connect with the person, not to win an argument. Light and short is best.

question.q: Qual opção resume melhor o texto?

options.text: Talking about the news can be light small talk; listen more, stay friendly, and keep it short.
You must read the news every single day to talk with North American clients.
North American people never want to talk about the news at work.
The best way to connect with people is to win every argument.

activities.title: Trade and Tariffs
activities.body:
Trade means countries buy and sell things to each other. One country may sell coffee, and another may sell cars. This is global trade.

Sometimes a country adds a tariff. A tariff is a tax on things that come from another country. It can make those things cost more money.

The supply chain is how a product travels from the factory to the store. Many people and trucks help move it. When trade or tariffs change, the supply chain can change too. These topics are common in the news, but keep your words simple and neutral.

question.q: Qual opção resume melhor o texto?

options.text: Trade is buying and selling between countries; a tariff is a tax, and both can affect the supply chain.
A tariff is a special kind of truck that moves products to the store.
Global trade only means countries selling coffee to each other.
The supply chain has nothing to do with trade or tariffs.

activities.title: Staying Neutral and Polite
activities.body:
Some news topics are sensitive. War, conflict, and politics can make people feel strong emotions. With a client, it is smart to stay neutral.

Neutral means you do not pick a side. You can listen and say, "That is interesting," or "I understand." You do not need to agree or argue.

If a topic feels too heavy, you can change it. You can talk about sports, food, or the weather. This keeps the conversation light and professional. A good rule is: be kind, be calm, and keep the relationship friendly.

question.q: Qual opção resume melhor o texto?

options.text: With sensitive news topics, stay neutral and polite, and change the subject if it gets too heavy.
You should always tell the client your strong opinion about war and politics.
The text is only about how to talk about the weather with a client.
Sensitive topics are easy and never cause strong emotions in people.

lessons.title: Tropicalização 1: structural choice — Brazil vs. US
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você explica ao cliente norte-americano por que a escolha estrutural no Brasil pode ser diferente da dos EUA, usando inglês simples para alinhar expectativas sobre concreto e aço.
lessons.overview:
In the United States, a steel structure is often the default choice. It is common practice there. But in Brazil, the equation is different. The material cost is different. The local labor is different. Here, concrete is often the best value. This is called tropicalization.

Why does the choice change? In Brazil, the local market has a strong concrete supply. The skilled workforce for concrete is large. So concrete can make sense and be a good fit. In the US, steel fabrication and supply availability are strong, so steel can win. The same project, two countries, two answers.

For Racional, this is a key point with the North American client. The client may expect steel, because that is normal at home. The contract manager must align expectations early. You explain: "The equation is different here." You show that concrete can be the right fit for Brazil. This avoids surprises and builds a strong, honest relationship.
lessons.intro:
O foco é alinhar expectativas: o que é padrão nos EUA pode não ser o melhor no Brasil. Retome a frase-âncora: "In the US, steel is the default. But here, the equation is different."

Lembre também de: "In Brazil, concrete is often the best value." e "Let me align expectations."
lessons.situation: O cliente norte-americano de um escritório esperava aço, como é padrão nos EUA. Você explica, com calma, por que no Brasil o concreto pode ser a melhor escolha.
lessons.context: In the US, steel is the default choice. It is common practice there. But in Brazil, the equation is different. The material cost and the local labor are different. Here, concrete is often the best value. Let me align expectations: for this project, concrete is the right fit.

Local labor for concrete is strong here.

Let me align expectations with you.

Concrete is the best value for this project.

lessons.title: Reinforced concrete in detail
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você descreve as etapas do concreto armado em inglês simples — fôrma, armadura, lançamento e cura — para acompanhar a execução e reportar o avanço ao cliente.
lessons.overview:
Reinforced concrete is concrete with steel inside. The steel bars are the rebar. The rebar gives the concrete strength. This is the most common structure in Brazil. Every contract manager must know its steps.

First, the team builds the formwork. This is the mold. Then they place the rebar inside. Next, they pour the concrete and vibrate it to remove air. After some hours, the concrete starts to set. Then it must cure for days to reach full compressive strength. Finally, the team can strip the formwork. We often use ready-mix concrete from a truck and a concrete pump to move it.

At Racional, this happens on almost every slab and column. On a hospital or a shopping center, quality control is key. We do a slump test to check the concrete mix. When you report to the client, you use these words: pour, cure, strength. Clear words show control and a safe project.
lessons.intro:
Vamos retomar a sequência do concreto: "We build the formwork, place the rebar, and pour the concrete."

Lembre também das etapas finais: "The concrete needs time to cure." e "Then we strip the formwork."
lessons.situation: Numa visita à obra de um shopping center, o cliente quer saber em que etapa está a laje. Você descreve o ciclo do concreto armado.
lessons.context: First, we build the formwork. Then we place the rebar inside. After that, we pour the concrete and vibrate it. The concrete needs time to set and cure. We do a slump test to check the mix. Next week, we strip the formwork.

vocab.example: The rebar goes inside the formwork.
The concrete must cure for days.
We do a slump test on site.
The concrete reaches full strength in 28 days.
We vibrate the concrete to remove air.
We strip the formwork next week.
We use a concrete pump for the slab.

lessons.title: Structural steel & prefabrication
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você descreve o uso de estrutura metálica e pré-fabricação em inglês simples — fabricação fora da obra, montagem com guindaste e ganho de prazo — para reportar o avanço ao cliente.
lessons.overview:
Structural steel is a fast way to build. The big idea is prefabrication. We make the steel parts in a fabrication shop, far from the site. This is off-site work. Then we bring the parts to the site. There we put them together. This is on-site work.

The parts are the steel beam and the steel column. We join them with a connection. Some connections use a bolt: we bolt the parts. Others use a weld. On site, a crane helps us lift the heavy parts. This is the steel erection. It is fast and clean.

For Racional, prefabrication brings a big schedule gain. A hyperscale data center for Amazon or Microsoft needs speed. With steel, we build off-site while the foundation cures on-site. Both jobs happen at the same time. When you report to the client, you can show this gain. Faster steel erection means an earlier handover. The client likes that.
lessons.intro:
Vamos retomar a lógica da pré-fabricação: "We make the parts off-site, then we erect them on-site."

Lembre do ganho de prazo: "Steel gives us a schedule gain." e da montagem: "The crane lifts the steel beams."
lessons.situation: O cliente norte-americano do data center quer acelerar a obra. Você explica como a estrutura metálica pré-fabricada traz ganho de prazo.
lessons.context: We use structural steel for speed. We make the parts off-site, in the fabrication shop. Then we bring them on-site. The crane lifts the steel beams and columns. We bolt the connections. This steel erection gives us a real schedule gain.

lessons.title: Formwork, shoring & temporary works
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você descreve, em inglês simples, os trabalhos temporários da estrutura — fôrma, escoramento e cimbramento — e diz com clareza ao cliente quando a fôrma pode sair e por que é seguro.
lessons.overview:
Every concrete structure starts with temporary works. The formwork is the mold for the wet concrete. The shoring holds the slab from below. These parts are not part of the final building, but the building cannot rise without them. At Racional, this happens on every project, from offices to hospitals to large data centers.

Temporary works are also safety works. Fresh concrete is weak. It needs time to cure and reach strength. If the shoring is bad, the slab can collapse. So the contract manager must watch the schedule and the load with great care. A clear plan keeps the team safe and keeps the project on time.

American clients always ask two simple questions on site: "Is it safe?" and "When can we strip the formwork?" A good answer joins the schedule and the safety in one sentence. This is daily language for a Racional contract manager, and clear English here builds trust with the client.
lessons.intro:
Esta é uma aula CORE (Módulo M3), do coração técnico do programa. O tema são os trabalhos temporários — fôrma, escoramento e cimbramento.

Duas frases-âncora para a prática:
"We can strip the formwork after the concrete reaches strength." (Podemos desformar depois que o concreto atinge a resistência.)
"The shoring supports the slab, and it is safe." (O escoramento sustenta a laje, e está seguro.)
lessons.situation: Visita de obra com o cliente americano. Vocês estão diante de uma laje recém-concretada, ainda escorada, e ele pergunta quando a fôrma pode sair.
lessons.context: This slab was poured on Monday. The formwork stays in place now. The shoring carries the load from below. The concrete needs more days to reach strength. We can strip the formwork next week, and it is fully safe.

lessons.title: Family trips & vacation stories
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você conta, em inglês simples, uma história curta de viagem em família ou férias e devolve a pergunta ao cliente americano para manter a conversa.
lessons.overview:
A big project at Racional can last 18 to 24 months. In that time, the American client becomes almost a colleague. Between formal meetings, people talk about real life. A family trip, a long weekend, or time at the beach are easy and warm topics. This small talk builds a real human bond.

Personal stories are powerful because they are honest. When you say the kids loved the trip, or that a few days off helped you recharge, the client sees the person behind the contract manager. This trust is useful later, in hard meetings about schedule or cost.

The goal here is simple. Tell a short and friendly story, and then return the question. Small talk is an exchange, not a long speech. A line like "How about you? Any travel plans?" keeps the conversation alive and shows you care about the other person too.
lessons.intro:
Esta é uma aula BRIDGE (Módulo M5) — de propósito mais leve e conversacional. O objetivo não é vocabulário técnico, e sim conexão humana.

Frases-âncora para a prática:
"We took a family trip to..." (Fizemos uma viagem em família para...)
"We had a great time." (Nos divertimos muito.)
"How about you? Any travel plans?" (E você? Algum plano de viagem?)
lessons.situation: Café antes da reunião semanal. O cliente americano pergunta sobre o seu feriado prolongado e a sua família.
lessons.context: We took a family trip to the coast last week. The kids loved the beach and we ate a lot of seafood. It was a nice break before this busy month. How about you? Any travel plans?

activities.title: A Road Trip in the United States
activities.body:
Many American families love a road trip. They put bags in the car and drive for many hours. Sometimes they drive for two or three days.

They stop to eat, to rest, and to see new places. Children play games in the car. Parents listen to music or talk about life.

A famous trip is Route 66. It is a very long, old road. People drive from town to town and take photos. A road trip is not only about the place. It is about the time together. The family talks, laughs, and has a great time.

question.q: Qual opção resume melhor o texto?

options.text: American families enjoy road trips, and the time together is as important as the destination.
Route 66 is the only good road for a family trip in the United States.
Children should always play quiet games when they travel in a car.
American families prefer to fly on planes instead of driving on long roads.

activities.title: Time Off at the Beach
activities.body:
When people take a break, many go to the beach. The beach is a warm and easy place to relax.

Families sit on the sand and look at the sea. Children make castles with sand and play in the water. Adults read books, sleep, or walk near the waves.

In the evening, the sky is orange and pink. Some families eat dinner outside and watch the sunset. They feel calm and happy. The beach is a simple way to rest, spend time with family, and forget about work for a few days.

question.q: Qual opção resume melhor o texto?

options.text: The beach is a relaxing place where families rest and spend happy time together.
Children only like the beach because they can build castles in the sand.
The best part of the beach is always the orange and pink sunset.
People should never bring books or work to the beach during a vacation.

activities.title: Telling a Travel Story
activities.body:
A travel story is a great way to talk with people. It is simple and warm.

First, you say where you went. For example: "Last year I went to the beach with my family." Then you say what you did. For example: "We swam, we ate good food, and we relaxed."

At the end, you say how you felt: "We had a great time." After your story, you ask a question back. You can say: "And you? Where do you like to travel?"

This small talk is friendly. It helps two people feel close, even in a short conversation.

question.q: Qual opção resume melhor o texto?

options.text: A short travel story plus a question back is a friendly way to connect with people.
You must always describe the food you ate when you tell a travel story.
Travel stories are only useful when you talk about a trip to the beach.
Asking questions is rude, so you should only talk about yourself.

lessons.title: MEP overview (Mechanical, Electrical, Plumbing)
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você apresenta, em inglês simples, a visão geral de MEP — sistemas mecânicos, elétricos e hidráulicos — e explica como você coordena os três para evitar interferências na obra.
lessons.overview:
MEP means three systems: mechanical, electrical and plumbing. Mechanical is air conditioning and ventilation. Electrical is power and panels. Plumbing is water and drainage. In offices, hospitals and data centers, these systems are the heart of the building. For a data center client like Microsoft or Amazon, MEP is the whole project.

The three systems share the same ceiling space. They cannot use the same place at the same time. When two systems hit the same spot, this is a clash. A clash on site means rework, delay and extra cost. So the team uses a 3D model to find clashes early, before installation.

For a Racional contract manager, the main job in MEP is not to install each system. The job is coordination. You make the three disciplines and their subcontractors work together. Clear English in these coordination meetings helps you avoid clashes and keep the schedule safe.
lessons.intro:
Esta é uma aula CORE (Módulo M3). MEP é um dos vocabulários mais importantes para você, sobretudo em data centers e hospitais.

Frases-âncora para a prática:
"MEP stands for mechanical, electrical and plumbing."
"We coordinate the systems to avoid clashes." (Coordenamos os sistemas para evitar interferências.)
lessons.situation: Reunião de coordenação com o cliente americano. Vocês revisam o modelo 3D e discutem como os sistemas MEP vão se acomodar no forro.
lessons.context: MEP stands for mechanical, electrical and plumbing. These three systems share the ceiling space, so we coordinate them with care. The 3D model helps us find clashes early, before installation on site.

lessons.title: Mechanical systems & HVAC
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você fala, em inglês simples, sobre os sistemas mecânicos e o HVAC — ar-condicionado, ventilação e resfriamento — e explica a importância da capacidade de resfriamento para o cliente.
lessons.overview:
The mechanical system controls the air inside a building. The short name is HVAC: heating, ventilation and air conditioning. It keeps the air clean, the temperature right and the rooms comfortable. In a hospital or an office, this means comfort. In a data center, this means survival.

A data center has many machines, and machines make a lot of heat. This heat is the heat load. The HVAC must remove it all day and all night. A chiller makes cold water for cooling. Ducts carry the cold air to each room. If the cooling capacity is too small, the machines get too hot and stop.

For clients like Microsoft, Amazon or Google, cooling is the number one topic. They ask about temperature, airflow and backup. A Racional contract manager must explain the HVAC plan in clear and simple English. When you say the system keeps the rooms cool day and night, the client feels safe.
lessons.intro:
Esta é uma aula CORE (Módulo M3). O tema são os sistemas mecânicos e o HVAC — central em data centers, onde resfriar é o assunto número um.

Frases-âncora para a prática:
"HVAC means heating, ventilation and air conditioning."
"The system keeps the rooms cool day and night." (O sistema mantém as salas frias dia e noite.)
lessons.situation: Reunião técnica com o cliente americano de um data center. Ele quer entender como o sistema de ar vai dar conta da carga térmica das máquinas.
lessons.context: The mechanical system controls the air in the building. HVAC means heating, ventilation and air conditioning. The chiller makes cold water for cooling. The ducts carry cold air to each room. The system keeps the machines cool day and night.

lessons.title: Electrical systems & substations
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você fala, em inglês simples, sobre o sistema elétrico e as subestações — fornecimento de energia, painéis, gerador de backup e redundância — e explica ao cliente como a energia chega segura ao prédio.
lessons.overview:
The electrical system brings power to the whole building. Power comes from the grid and enters through a substation. The substation lowers the voltage to a safe level. Then the switchgear and the panels distribute power to every floor and every room. Without power, nothing works.

In a hospital or a data center, power can never stop. A power cut is a serious risk. So the design uses a backup generator and redundancy. Redundancy means there is always a second path for the power. If one path fails, the other keeps the building alive. This is why data center clients ask so many questions about power.

For a Racional contract manager, the electrical system is a top priority. Clients like Microsoft and Amazon want to know about the power supply, the backup and the risk of an outage. Clear and simple English helps you explain that the design is safe and has no single point of failure.
lessons.intro:
Esta é uma aula CORE (Módulo M3). O tema é o sistema elétrico e as subestações — crítico em hospitais e data centers, onde a energia não pode parar.

Frases-âncora para a prática:
"The substation supplies power to the building."
"We have a backup generator for redundancy." (Temos um gerador de backup para redundância.)
lessons.situation: Reunião com o cliente americano de um data center. Ele quer entender como a energia chega ao prédio e o que acontece se a rede cair.
lessons.context: The substation takes power from the grid. It supplies power to the whole building. The switchgear and the panels distribute the power to each floor. We have a backup generator for redundancy. If the grid fails, the building still has power.

vocab.example: The electrical system feeds the building.

Each floor has its own panel.

Redundancy gives us a second power path.
We energize the panel after the test.
The backup stops any outage risk.
