lessons.title: Plumbing & hydraulics
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você fala, em inglês simples, sobre o sistema hidráulico — abastecimento de água, tubos, válvulas, drenagem e testes de pressão — e explica ao cliente que tudo está testado antes de fechar as paredes.
lessons.overview:
The plumbing system moves water through the building. The water supply brings clean water in. Pipes carry the water, and valves open and close the flow. The drainage takes used water and sewage out. In offices, hospitals and shopping centers, this system serves people every day.

The biggest risk in plumbing is a leak. A small leak inside a wall can cause big damage later. So the team runs a pressure test on every pipe. If the water pressure stays stable, there is no leak. This test happens before the team closes the walls, because a leak behind a finished wall is very hard and costly to fix.

For a Racional contract manager, the rule is simple and strong: test first, close the walls later. American clients value this discipline. When you explain in clear English that every pipe passed the pressure test before the walls were closed, the client trusts your quality control.
lessons.intro:
Esta é uma aula CORE (Módulo M3). O tema é o sistema hidráulico — tubos, válvulas, drenagem e, acima de tudo, o teste de pressão antes de fechar as paredes.

Frases-âncora para a prática:
"We run a pressure test before we close the walls."
"The pipes passed the test, with no leak." (Os tubos passaram no teste, sem vazamento.)
lessons.situation: Inspeção de qualidade com o cliente americano. Vocês conferem a tubulação no forro antes de a equipe fechar as paredes.
lessons.context: The plumbing system brings water to the building. The pipes carry the water and the valves control the flow. The drainage takes the used water out. We run a pressure test on every pipe. There is no leak, so we can close the walls now.

lessons.title: American humor, idioms & slang
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você vai entender gírias, expressões (idioms) e o humor do cliente americano e responder com leveza, sem se perder na conversa.
lessons.overview:
American clients talk in a friendly way. They use slang and idioms every day. An idiom is a phrase with a hidden meaning. "It's a piece of cake" does not talk about cake. It means something is very easy. You hear these phrases on the job site and in meetings.

American humor is often light. People make jokes about themselves. They use sarcasm too. You do not need to make jokes. You only need to understand and smile. This helps you build trust with the client. At Racional, your clients are from the United States. They run big projects like offices, hospitals, and data centers for Microsoft, Amazon, and Google.

When you understand slang, the talk feels easy. You can say "no worries" or "let's wrap up." If you do not understand a word, you can ask: "What does that mean?" Americans like to explain. This small question makes the relationship stronger and warmer.
lessons.intro:
Esta é uma aula BRIDGE (Módulo M6), de repertório cultural. O foco é entender o cliente americano quando ele usa gírias e idioms.

Relembre três frases-âncora: "It's a piece of cake" (é muito fácil), "Let's touch base tomorrow" (vamos nos alinhar amanhã) e "We're on the same page" (estamos alinhados). E a regra de ouro: se não entendeu, pergunte "What does that mean?"
lessons.situation: Fim de um dia puxado de obra. O cliente americano relaxa, solta algumas gírias e faz uma piada leve. Você acompanha o clima.
lessons.context: Good work today. That was a piece of cake for your team. Let's call it a day. We can touch base tomorrow. I think we are on the same page on the schedule. No worries about the rest.

vocab.example: Americans use a lot of slang.

We are on the same page.
It is late. Let's call it a day.
No worries, we can fix it.
Your team is on the ball.
He likes to crack a joke.

practiceBank.title: Fim de obra: cliente solta uma gíria

O professor (cliente americano) usa 'let's call it a day', 'no worries' e 'a piece of cake'; o aluno responde com leveza e pede sentido quando não entende ('What does that mean?'). O aluno deve manter o clima descontraído e usar pelo menos 4 expressões da aula. Professor observa e devolve novas gírias.

practiceBank.title: O que isso quer dizer?
practiceBank.how: Professor dispara idioms da aula em ritmo rápido ('on the same page', 'on the ball', 'heads-up', 'ballpark') e o aluno explica em inglês simples o sentido e dá um exemplo de obra. Inverter: o aluno dispara e o professor responde. Foco em produção oral imediata sem travar.

practiceBank.title: Recap leve do dia
practiceBank.how: O aluno grava 60 segundos contando como foi o dia na obra usando 'to wrap up', 'to call it a day' e 'to touch base' com o cliente amanhã. Deve soar natural e descontraído. Professor escuta depois e marca onde as expressões soaram forçadas ou naturais.

O aluno faz perguntas curtas usando os idioms para 'preencher' cada linha, simulando vários colegas que o professor encarna. Produção: formular perguntas com as expressões estudadas.

practiceBank.title: Humor americano em reunião: ajuda ou atrapalha?
practiceBank.how: O aluno defende em inglês se trocar piadas ('to crack a joke') com o cliente americano cria rapport ou se é arriscado em obra séria. Deve usar 'on the same page', 'no worries' e justificar com situações reais do data center. Professor faz de advogado do diabo.

practiceBank.title: Defina sem dizer a palavra

practiceBank.title: Do PT pro idiom certo
practiceBank.how: Professor diz em português ('vamos encerrar por hoje', 'me avisa antes', 'estamos alinhados') e o aluno responde imediatamente com o idiom inglês equivalente em frase completa de obra. Ritmo de corrida. Foco em ativar 'call it a day', 'heads-up', 'on the same page'.

practiceBank.title: Mini-call de alinhamento
practiceBank.how: Aluno simula uma ligação curta para 'touch base' com o cliente e confirmar que estão 'on the same page' sobre o cronograma do data center, fechando com 'let's wrap up'. Deve encaixar 5 expressões naturalmente. Professor responde como cliente e cobra fluidez.

practiceBank.title: Um minuto sobre gírias americanas

practiceBank.title: Aluno vira o americano descontraído
practiceBank.how: O aluno encarna o cliente americano relaxado no fim do dia, soltando gírias e uma piada leve; o professor faz o engenheiro brasileiro que pede esclarecimentos. O aluno precisa produzir as expressões com tom natural e timing de humor. Inverte a perspectiva.

practiceBank.title: Encerra a cena com o idiom

pill.region: Frase longa: pausa antes da relativa
pill.tip: Antes de uma cláusula explicativa, faça leve pausa para separar o bloco. Em 'The vendor, / who arrived late, / missed the briefing', as pausas em torno de 'who arrived late' mostram que é informação extra.

activities.title: What Is an Idiom?
activities.body:
An idiom is a group of words with a hidden meaning. The words alone do not tell you the true idea. For example, "it's a piece of cake" is not about cake. It means a job is very easy. "Break a leg" is not a bad wish. It means "good luck!"

Americans use idioms every day. You hear them at work, at home, and on TV. At first they sound strange. But do not worry. With time and practice, you learn them. Soon you will use idioms too, and English will feel more natural.

question.q: Qual opção resume melhor o texto?

options.text: Idioms are phrases with a hidden meaning, and you learn them with practice over time.
"It's a piece of cake" is the only American idiom you need to know.
Americans never use idioms when they talk at work or at home.
Cooking cake is a popular hobby in American homes today.

activities.title: Slang at Work
activities.body:
Slang is very informal language. Friends and coworkers use it to sound relaxed. When something is good, an American may say "that's cool" or "awesome." If a person makes a mistake, you can say "no worries" to stay friendly.

At the end of a long day, people say "let's call it a day." This means it is time to stop working. To plan a quick talk later, they say "let's touch base." Slang is not rude. It shows you are part of the team. Listen first, and use it little by little.

question.q: Qual opção resume melhor o texto?

options.text: Slang is friendly, informal language at work, and you can start using it slowly.
Slang is rude language that you must never use with coworkers.
"Let's call it a day" is the only slang phrase used in American offices.
American workers prefer to talk only in very formal English all day.

activities.title: American Humor Is Light
activities.body:
Americans often use light, friendly humor. They make small jokes in meetings or on the job site. This helps people relax and feel close. A short joke can break the ice before serious work begins.

You do not need to be funny too. Just smile and answer with ease. If you do not understand a joke, you can say, "Good one!" or ask kindly, "What do you mean?" Most people are happy to explain. Humor is a way to build a good relationship. Stay calm, be friendly, and enjoy the talk.

question.q: Qual opção resume melhor o texto?

options.text: American humor is light and friendly, and you can relax, smile, and ask if a joke is unclear.
You must always tell funny jokes to work with American clients.
American humor only happens at the start of very serious meetings.
It is rude to ask an American what a joke means.

lessons.title: Fire protection systems
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você vai descrever os sistemas de proteção contra incêndio de uma obra (sprinklers, bomba, alarme) em inglês simples, com o cliente americano.
lessons.overview:
Every building needs a fire protection system. This system keeps people safe. It has two parts. Active protection uses water and alarms to fight a fire. Passive protection uses walls and doors to stop the fire and smoke. Both parts work together.

The active system has sprinklers, a fire pump, and a fire alarm. A smoke detector finds smoke fast. Then the sprinklers start and the pump pushes water through the pipes. The passive system has fire doors and fireproofing on the steel. A fire compartment holds the fire in one area.

At Racional, fire protection is very important. Hospitals, shopping centers, and data centers for Amazon, Microsoft, and Google all need strong systems. The American client asks many questions about this. You must talk about sprinklers, pumps, and the fire rating of each part. Clear words here build trust and keep the project safe.
lessons.intro:
Esta é uma aula CORE (Módulo M3), o coração técnico. Foco: o sistema de proteção contra incêndio.

Relembre três frases-âncora: "The system has sprinklers and a fire pump" (o sistema tem sprinklers e bomba), "The smoke detector starts the alarm" (o detector aciona o alarme) e "We test the fire pump every month" (testamos a bomba todo mês).
lessons.situation: Visita do cliente americano à obra de um data center. Ele pergunta como funciona a proteção contra incêndio do prédio.
lessons.context: Our building has a full fire protection system. The smoke detector finds smoke fast. Then the alarm starts. The sprinklers open and the fire pump pushes water. Fire doors stop the smoke. We test the pump every month.

vocab.example: The building has a fire protection system.
The sprinkler opens and drops water.
The fire pump pushes the water.
There is a hydrant on each floor.
The fire alarm is very loud.
The smoke detector finds smoke fast.
The fire door stops the smoke.
We add fireproofing on the steel.
The fire compartment holds the fire.
The pump helps to fight a fire.
This door has a two-hour fire rating.

lessons.title: Tropicalização 2: fire code — corpo de bombeiros (BR)
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você vai explicar ao cliente americano por que o projeto de incêndio segue o corpo de bombeiros (fire code) brasileiro e como obtemos a aprovação.
lessons.overview:
In Brazil, the fire department controls fire safety. They make the rules. We call these rules the fire code. Every building must follow this code. The team makes a fire project and sends it to the fire department. This is part of "tropicalização": we adapt the American design to the Brazilian rules.

The fire department checks the project. Then they do a fire inspection on the site. If everything is right, they give the operating permit. Without this permit, the building cannot open. So we must comply with every code requirement. If they find a problem, they write a finding, and we fix it.

This is very important for Racional. The American client knows the rules from the United States. But Brazil is different. The Brazilian standard can differ from the American one. Your job is to bridge the gap. You explain the local rules in simple English. This keeps the project legal and on time for offices, hospitals, and data centers.
lessons.intro:
Esta é uma aula CORE (Módulo M3), de tropicalização. Foco: o fire code brasileiro e o corpo de bombeiros.

Relembre três frases-âncora: "We must comply with the local fire code" (precisamos seguir o código local), "The fire department gives the operating permit" (o corpo de bombeiros dá a licença de funcionamento) e "The Brazilian standard differs from the American one" (a norma brasileira difere da americana).
lessons.situation: Reunião com o cliente americano. Ele estranha o processo de incêndio do Brasil e você explica como funciona o corpo de bombeiros.
lessons.context: In Brazil, the fire department makes the rules. We must comply with the local fire code. We send a fire project to them. They do an inspection on site. Then they give the operating permit. Without it, the building cannot open.

vocab.example: We follow the local fire code.
The fire department makes the rules.
We need the operating permit to open.
We send the fire project to them.
The fire inspection is next week.
We must comply with the code.
Our rules differ from the US rules.

lessons.title: Building envelope & facade
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você vai descrever a fachada e o envelope do prédio (curtain wall, vidro, vedação) e falar de testes de estanqueidade com o cliente americano.
lessons.overview:
The building envelope is the skin of the building. It is the wall between the inside and the outside. The facade is the front face that people see. A good envelope keeps the rain, the heat, and the noise outside. It protects the people inside.

Many buildings use a curtain wall. This is a light wall of glazing (glass) and metal. The mullion holds the glass. Other buildings use cladding on the wall. We add sealant for weatherproofing. We also test for airtightness and good thermal performance, so the building saves energy.

For Racional, the facade is very important. Office towers and data centers for Microsoft and Amazon need a strong, clean envelope. Before we install all the glass, we build a mock-up. Then we do a water test. If we find a leak, we fix it first. This protects the client and keeps the project on schedule.
lessons.intro:
Esta é uma aula CORE (Módulo M3), técnica. Foco: o envelope e a fachada do prédio.

Relembre três frases-âncora: "The curtain wall has glass and metal" (o curtain wall tem vidro e metal), "We do a water test on the mock-up" (fazemos teste de água no protótipo) e "There is no leak" (não há vazamento).
lessons.situation: O cliente americano visita a obra de uma torre de escritórios e quer entender como a fachada de vidro é testada.
lessons.context: The facade is the skin of the building. We use a curtain wall with glass and metal. First we build a mock-up. Then we do a water test. We check for leaks. We add sealant for weatherproofing. The building stays dry inside.

lessons.title: Vertical transportation (elevators, traffic study)
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você vai falar sobre transporte vertical (elevadores, escadas rolantes, estudo de tráfego) e tempo de espera com o cliente americano.
lessons.overview:
Vertical transportation moves people up and down the building. The main parts are the elevator and the escalator. In a tall office tower or a hospital, this is very important. People do not like to wait. A long waiting time makes the client unhappy.

Before we choose the elevators, we do a traffic study. This study looks at the peak hour, when many people arrive at the same time. It checks the capacity and the speed of each car. The elevator car goes up and down inside the hoistway. The machine room holds the motor. We want a fast and smooth ride.

For Racional, this is key in big projects. Office towers and shopping centers for American clients need elevators that handle heavy traffic. At the end, we do the commissioning. We test every car and check the waiting time. A good system makes the building work well and keeps the client happy.
lessons.intro:
Esta é uma aula CORE (Módulo M3), técnica. Foco: transporte vertical e estudo de tráfego.

Relembre três frases-âncora: "We do a traffic study first" (fazemos o estudo de tráfego antes), "The waiting time is short" (o tempo de espera é curto) e "The elevator has a smooth ride" (o elevador tem viagem suave).
lessons.situation: O cliente americano pergunta como os elevadores da torre vão aguentar o horário de pico com muita gente.
lessons.context: Vertical transportation moves people up and down. First we do a traffic study. It checks the peak hour. We look at the capacity and the speed of each car. We want a short waiting time and a smooth ride. Then we do the commissioning.

vocab.example: We do a traffic study first.

lessons.title: Music talk 3: Lenny Kravitz — rock, funk & guitar legends
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você vai conversar sobre música — rock, funk e Lenny Kravitz — para criar conexão e rapport com o cliente americano.
lessons.overview:
Music is a great way to connect with people. This is a Music Talk lesson. Today the artist is Lenny Kravitz. He is an American singer and a famous guitar player. He mixes rock and funk. His songs have a strong groove and a great vibe.

When you talk about music, the client relaxes. You can say a band has a good riff or a great guitar solo. You can talk about a favorite album or a big hit. You do not need hard words. Simple sentences work very well: "I love this song" or "This album is unforgettable."

For Racional, this matters a lot. A project with an American client can take 18 to 24 months. You meet the client many times. Small talk about music builds a long and warm relationship. Lenny Kravitz is a safe and fun topic. It helps you go from a work talk to a real human connection.
lessons.intro:
Esta é uma aula BRIDGE (Módulo M5), da trilha Music Talk. Foco: conversar sobre música para criar rapport.

Relembre três frases-âncora: "I love this song" (eu amo essa música), "He is a great guitar player" (ele é um ótimo guitarrista) e "This album is unforgettable" (esse álbum é inesquecível).
lessons.situation: Pausa do café com o cliente americano. Sai uma música do Lenny Kravitz e vocês começam a conversar sobre rock e funk.
lessons.context: I like Lenny Kravitz a lot. He is a great guitar player. He mixes rock and funk. His songs have a strong groove. This album is unforgettable. I love the guitar solo. Let's turn it up!

practiceBank.how: O aluno grava 60 segundos recomendando um hit de rock ou funk ao cliente americano, explicando o vibe, o riff e por que é unforgettable. Deve soar natural e empolgado. Professor escuta e comenta se daria vontade de 'turn it up'.

practiceBank.title: Descreva a banda no palco
practiceBank.how: Com uma foto de banda de rock, o aluno descreve em voz alta o guitar player, o bass, os drums e o clima do show, usando groove e vibe. Professor aponta um músico e pede mais detalhes. Vocabulário em ação na descrição.

practiceBank.title: Conversa de música rápida
practiceBank.how: Professor faz perguntas leves ('favorite riff?', 'rock or funk?', 'best guitar solo?') e o aluno responde em frases curtas e naturais. Inverter papéis. Foco em manter a conversa fluindo para rapport, ativando o vocabulário da aula.

practiceBank.title: Gostos musicais do escritório
practiceBank.how: Professor entrega uma lista ('alguém que ama um bom guitar solo', 'que mistura styles', 'que aumenta o som no carro') e o aluno faz perguntas usando os termos para 'preencher' cada linha, com o professor encarnando vários colegas. Produção de perguntas leves.

practiceBank.title: Aluno vira o americano fã de rock
practiceBank.how: O aluno encarna o cliente americano apaixonado por Lenny Kravitz e puxa a conversa sobre riff, groove e álbuns; o professor responde como o engenheiro. O aluno produz o tema musical com naturalidade e timing. Inverte a perspectiva.

practiceBank.title: Top 3 lendas da guitarra
practiceBank.how: O aluno monta um top 3 de guitar players/lendas e justifica cada escolha em inglês citando riff, guitar solo e vibe. Professor discorda para puxar conversa. Opinião descontraída com o vocabulário da aula para criar rapport.

practiceBank.title: Um minuto sobre rock e funk
practiceBank.how: O aluno fala 60 segundos sem parar sobre por que rock e funk combinam (como faz Lenny Kravitz), usando to mix styles, groove e riff. Se travar, professor dá uma carta com novo termo. Foco em fluência e descontração.

practiceBank.title: Trocando indicações por áudio
practiceBank.how: Sem se olhar, aluno e professor trocam recomendações musicais como numa call de áudio: o aluno descreve um hit pelo som (riff, groove, drums) e o professor tenta adivinhar a música. Produção descritiva oral sem apoio visual.

practiceBank.title: A música que mudou o clima
practiceBank.how: Professor começa cenas ('Estávamos cansados na obra, aí tocou aquele riff e...') e para; o aluno completa contando como o vibe mudou e a vontade de 'turn it up'. Várias cenas. Produção rápida e leve com o vocabulário musical.

pill.tip: No telefone, americanos colam o pronome ao verbo: 'I will' vira "I'll" (soa 'áiou', um som só) e 'we are' vira "we're" (soa 'uír'). Falar separado soa robótico.
pill.sample: I'll send the file now, and we're ready to start the call.

activities.intro: Antes de uma reunião com o cliente americano do projeto do Hospital, é comum ter um momento de small talk. Falar de música é uma ótima maneira de criar conexão. Monte um pequeno pitch sobre por que você gosta de Lenny Kravitz e de rock/funk. Use cada passo abaixo como um degrau e fale frases simples (A1+).

activities.model: I like music a lot. After work at Racional, I listen to music at home. I like rock and funk because the groove is very good. My favorite is Lenny Kravitz. He is a great guitar player, and he mixes many styles. I love the riff in his songs. Do you like rock too? We can talk about music before our meeting.

wrapUp.prompt: Agora faça o pitch ao professor SEM ler. Imagine que é o começo de uma call com o cliente do Hospital.
wrapUp.model: Hi! Before we start, I want to talk a little. I like rock and funk. My favorite is Lenny Kravitz. He is a great guitar player and he mixes styles. Do you like music too?
wrapUp.teacherNote: Foque em fluidez, não em perfeição. Corrija só 'I like / he plays / he mixes'. Elogie o uso de groove, riff, guitar player.

activities.title: Who Is Lenny Kravitz?
activities.body:
Lenny Kravitz is an American musician. He was born in New York in 1964. His mother was an actress and his father worked in television. Music was always around him.

Lenny sings, and he is also a great guitar player. He plays many instruments, like drums and bass. He often makes his songs alone in the studio.

He mixes rock and funk. His music has a strong groove and a cool vibe. Famous songs are "Are You Gonna Go My Way" and "Fly Away." People around the world love his energy and his style.

question.q: Qual opção resume melhor o texto?

options.text: Lenny Kravitz is an American musician and guitar player who mixes rock and funk and is loved around the world.
Lenny Kravitz was born in New York in 1964.
American music is the most popular music in the world today.
Lenny Kravitz only plays the drums in a famous rock band.

activities.title: Rock and Funk
activities.body:
Rock and funk are two music styles from the United States. Rock music is loud and strong. It uses electric guitar, bass, and drums. A guitar riff is a short part that repeats and that people remember.

Funk music is about the groove. The bass and the drums work together so you want to dance. James Brown is called the "King of Funk."

Many artists mix rock and funk. Lenny Kravitz is one of them. When you mix styles, the music feels fresh and full of energy. This mix gives his songs a special vibe.

question.q: Qual opção resume melhor o texto?

options.text: Rock and funk are two American styles, and some artists like Lenny Kravitz mix them for fresh energy.
A guitar riff is a short part that repeats in a song.
Music with electric guitars is always better than other music.
James Brown taught Lenny Kravitz how to play the guitar.

activities.title: Guitar Legends
activities.body:
The guitar is a very important instrument in rock music. Some guitar players are legends. People still talk about them today.

Jimi Hendrix is one of the most famous. He played in new and surprising ways. Many people say he is the best guitar player ever. Other legends are Eric Clapton, B.B. King, and Chuck Berry.

Lenny Kravitz loves these old artists. He learns from them, but he also creates his own sound. A great guitar player needs practice, feeling, and a good groove. The guitar can be soft or very powerful.

question.q: Qual opção resume melhor o texto?

options.text: The guitar is central to rock, and legends like Jimi Hendrix inspire players such as Lenny Kravitz.
Jimi Hendrix is the most famous guitar player in the world.
The guitar is the only instrument used in all rock music.
Lenny Kravitz wants to sound exactly like Eric Clapton.

lessons.title: Architectural finishes
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você vai saber falar, em inglês simples, sobre acabamentos arquitetônicos e padrão de entrega em uma reunião de obra com o cliente.
lessons.overview:
Architectural finishes are the last layer of a building. They are the parts people see and touch every day: the flooring, the ceiling, the paint, the doors and frames, and the tile in the bathrooms. The structure holds the building up, but the finishes give the building its quality and its look. For a Racional client, the finishes are the first thing they notice when they walk in.

Finishes are very important for the contract manager. The finish schedule is a list that shows the material for each room. It tells you which flooring, which paint, and which tile to use. Good workmanship means the work is clean and well done. On a corporate office for an American client, the level of finish must be high, because the client will use that space for important meetings.

Many Racional projects start with a model floor. This is one floor finished first, so the client can see and approve the quality. After the client approves the sample and the model floor, the team builds all the other floors to match it. Small problems happen, so the team does touch-up work at the end. Clear talk about finishes keeps the client happy and protects the final delivery.
lessons.intro:
Hoje você vai praticar como falar dos acabamentos e do padrão de entrega com o cliente americano. Frases-âncora: "This is the finish schedule for the model floor.", "The new floors will match the sample." e "We will do the touch-up before delivery."

Use frases curtas, uma ideia por frase. Aponte para o material e diga o nome em inglês.
lessons.situation: Você está mostrando o pavimento-modelo (model floor) ao representante do cliente americano. Ele quer confirmar o padrão de acabamento antes de liberar os outros andares.
lessons.context: This is the model floor. Here you can see the finishes. The flooring is ready and the paint is done. The doors and frames are new. This is the finish schedule for this floor. The other floors will match this sample. We will do a small touch-up before we hand over the floor. The workmanship is clean and the level of finish is high.

vocab.example: The flooring is new and clean.
The ceiling is white and high.
We need one more partition here.
The paint is done in this room.
The doors and frames are new.
The millwork is in the meeting room.
This is the finish schedule for the floor.

vocab.pt: mão de obra, qualidade do acabamento

vocab.example: The level of finish is high here.
We start with the model floor.
We will do a small touch-up.
The tile is ready in the bathroom.

exercises.title: 1. Associe o termo em inglês ao significado em português
exercises.explanation: Esses quatro termos guiam a aula: o material (flooring), a lista (finish schedule), o andar de referência (model floor) e o ajuste final (touch-up).

exercises.title: 2. Escolha a frase correta
exercises.prompt: Você quer dizer ao cliente que os outros andares vão ficar iguais ao pavimento-modelo. O que você diz?

options.text: The other floors will match the model floor.
The other floors are the ceiling.
options.whyWrong: Ceiling é teto; aqui você fala de igualar o padrão, não do teto.

options.text: We will paint the sample.
options.whyWrong: Sample é a amostra de aprovação; não é o que você vai pintar.

exercises.title: 3. Complete a frase
exercises.prompt: This is the ___ for the model floor. It lists every material.
exercises.explanation: "Finish schedule" = a tabela que mostra o acabamento de cada ambiente.

exercises.title: 4. Escreva sua resposta ao cliente
exercises.prompt: Escreva 2 frases curtas dizendo que o pavimento-modelo está pronto e que os outros andares vão ficar iguais. Use ao menos 2 termos da aula em inglês.
exercises.modelAnswer: The model floor is ready. The flooring and the paint are done. The other floors will match this sample.
exercises.explanation: A correção olha só o uso dos termos: mostre que você sabe falar do padrão de acabamento e da igualdade entre os andares.

exercises.title: 5. Leia em voz alta
exercises.targetText: This is the model floor. The other floors will match this sample.
exercises.translation: Este é o pavimento-modelo. Os outros andares vão ficar iguais a esta amostra.
exercises.prompt: Você está com o cliente americano no andar-modelo. Fale com calma, apontando para o acabamento.
exercises.explanation: Duas ideias curtas: primeiro o que é o andar, depois a promessa de igualdade. Pausa no ponto.

lessons.critical: Em voz alta, por 15 a 20 segundos, mostre ao cliente o pavimento-modelo, diga que o piso e a pintura estão prontos, que os outros andares vão ficar iguais à amostra e que você fará o retoque antes da entrega. Use "model floor", "flooring" e "touch-up".
takeaways: I can name the main finishes of a building.
I can show a model floor to a client.
I can say the other floors will match the sample.
I can talk about touch-up before we hand over.

practiceBank.title: Tour do pavimento-modelo com o cliente americano
practiceBank.how: O aluno é o engenheiro guiando o cliente (professor) pelo model floor. Ele descreve cada acabamento (flooring, ceiling, partition, doors and frames, millwork) usando 'level of finish' e 'workmanship'. O professor faz perguntas para confirmar o padrão antes de liberar os outros andares e corrige só no fim.

practiceBank.title: Descreva o finish schedule
practiceBank.how: O professor mostra (ou descreve) uma planilha de finish schedule por ambiente. O aluno fala em voz alta o acabamento de cada espaço ('In the lobby, the flooring is tile; the ceiling is...'), usando 'paint', 'tile', 'millwork', 'partition'. O professor cobra precisão e completude.

practiceBank.title: Dois andares, dois padrões
practiceBank.how: Aluno e professor têm cada um a ficha de acabamento de um andar diferente. Sem ver a do outro, eles fazem perguntas ('What's the flooring on floor 3?') para descobrir as diferenças de 'level of finish'. O aluno produz perguntas e respostas usando o vocab de acabamentos.

practiceBank.title: Touch-up ou sample?
practiceBank.how: O professor cita um defeito de acabamento (mancha na pintura, junta de tile torta, workmanship ruim numa porta). O aluno decide e diz se pede 'touch-up', um novo 'sample' ou rejeita o 'level of finish', justificando em inglês. Foco em usar os termos no contexto certo.

practiceBank.title: Padrão de entrega em 60 segundos
practiceBank.how: O aluno grava 60s explicando ao cliente qual é o 'level of finish' acordado e por que o 'workmanship' do model floor representa o padrão dos demais andares. Deve encaixar pelo menos 6 termos da aula. O professor ouve e devolve 2 ajustes.

practiceBank.title: Perguntas rápidas sobre acabamentos
practiceBank.how: Professor e aluno alternam perguntas rápidas de obra ('Is the millwork approved?', 'When do we do the touch-up?'). O aluno responde em uma frase curta e devolve outra pergunta, mantendo o ritmo. Treina fluência com o vocab de finishes.

practiceBank.title: Cliente reprovou o acabamento
practiceBank.how: O cliente (professor) diz que o 'workmanship' das partitions e doors and frames está abaixo do esperado. O aluno conduz a conversa: reconhece, propõe 'touch-up' ou novo 'sample', renegocia o 'level of finish' e cronograma. Produção de linguagem de negociação técnica.

practiceBank.title: Prioridade de acabamentos antes da entrega
practiceBank.how: O aluno lista 6 itens de finish (flooring, paint, ceiling, millwork, tile, doors) e os ordena por prioridade para concluir antes da liberação dos andares, justificando cada escolha em inglês. O professor desafia a ordem para gerar mais produção.

practiceBank.title: Fale um minuto sobre o model floor
practiceBank.how: O aluno fala sem parar por 60s sobre o model floor e seus acabamentos, sem grandes pausas nem repetições. Se travar, recomeça. O professor conta o tempo e marca quantos termos da aula apareceram naturalmente.

practiceBank.title: Antes e depois do touch-up
practiceBank.how: O professor descreve duas versões do mesmo ambiente (antes e depois do touch-up: pintura, tile, ceiling). O aluno descreve as diferenças em inglês ('Now the paint is even; the tile is aligned'), usando 'workmanship' e 'level of finish'. Foco em descrição comparativa.

practiceBank.title: Engenheiro na berlinda sobre o acabamento
practiceBank.how: O aluno senta na 'cadeira quente' e o professor (cliente) dispara perguntas duras sobre o finish schedule, o workmanship e os samples. O aluno responde sem hesitar, defendendo o padrão de entrega. Treina resposta rápida sob pressão.

practiceBank.title: Cliente reclama por e-mail do acabamento
practiceBank.how: O professor lê um e-mail curto do cliente apontando problemas de acabamento. O aluno responde oralmente como se estivesse no telefone: confirma o que vai corrigir (touch-up), reagenda a inspeção do model floor e reafirma o level of finish. Produção de resposta estruturada.

pill.tip: Ao soletrar nomes na ligação, use o alfabeto OTAN: A é "Alpha" (ÁL-fa), B é "Bravo" (BRÁ-vou). A tônica cai na primeira sílaba das duas.

lessons.title: Office towers & corporate buildings
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você vai saber falar, em inglês simples, sobre torres de escritórios, área e eficiência de planta para um cliente corporativo.
lessons.overview:
An office tower is a tall corporate building with many floors. Big companies rent space in these towers for their teams. Racional builds high-quality office towers for important clients in São Paulo and other cities. Each floor must be ready for work, with good light, good air, and a clean look.

Two numbers matter a lot in an office tower. The first is the gross area, which is the total area of the floor. The second is the net leasable area, which is the area the company can really use and pay for. The relation between them is the efficiency. A good floor plate with a small core gives more usable space, so the client is happy. An open floor plan also helps teams work together.

Many American clients want a Class A building with LEED certification. Class A means top quality. LEED means the building is green and saves energy. These features help the client find a good tenant and lease the space fast. When Racional can target high efficiency and a strong certification, the project has more value for everyone.
lessons.intro:
Hoje você vai praticar como falar de área, eficiência e padrão de um edifício corporativo. Frases-âncora: "This floor has high efficiency.", "The core is small, so the net area is large." e "This is a Class A building with LEED certification."

Use frases curtas e números simples. Uma ideia por frase.
lessons.situation: Você apresenta um andar da torre corporativa a um cliente americano. Ele quer entender a eficiência da planta e o padrão do edifício antes de fechar a locação.
lessons.context: Welcome to our office tower. This is a Class A building. The gross area of this floor is large. The core is small, so the net leasable area is high. This gives us good efficiency. We have an open floor plan for your teams. The building also has LEED certification. You can lease this floor and start fast.

vocab.example: This office tower has thirty floors.
This is a modern corporate building.
This floor is ready for your team.
The gross area is very large.
The net leasable area is high here.
The floor plate is open and clear.
The core is small and central.
We have an open floor plan here.
This is a Class A building.
We want a good tenant for this floor.
You can lease this floor today.

exercises.title: 1. Ouça e escreva a frase
exercises.correctText: This floor has good efficiency.
exercises.explanation: Frase curta e direta para destacar a qualidade da planta ao cliente.

exercises.title: 2. Coloque as palavras na ordem correta
exercises.explanation: Ordem básica: sujeito + verbo + complemento. "This is a Class A building."

exercises.title: 3. Complete a frase
exercises.prompt: The core is small, so the ___ is high.
exercises.explanation: Núcleo pequeno (small core) deixa mais espaço útil, ou seja, mais net leasable area.

exercises.title: 4. Escolha a frase correta
exercises.prompt: Você quer dizer ao cliente que o edifício é verde e economiza energia. O que você diz?

options.text: The building has a small core.
options.whyWrong: Isso fala da planta, não da certificação verde.

options.text: The building has LEED certification.
You can lease the tenant.
options.whyWrong: Tenant é o locatário; você não aluga o locatário, você aluga o andar.

exercises.title: 5. Leia em voz alta
exercises.targetText: This is a Class A building. You can lease this floor and start fast.
exercises.translation: Este é um edifício classe A. Você pode alugar este andar e começar rápido.
exercises.prompt: Você está com o cliente americano no andar. Fale com confiança e tom comercial leve.
exercises.explanation: Duas ideias curtas: o padrão do edifício e o benefício prático para o cliente.

lessons.critical: Em voz alta, por 15 a 20 segundos, apresente o andar ao cliente: diga que é um edifício classe A, que o núcleo é pequeno e a área útil é alta, e que ele pode alugar e começar rápido. Use "Class A building", "net leasable area" e "efficiency".
takeaways: I can describe an office tower to a client.
I can talk about gross area and net leasable area.
I can explain floor efficiency in a simple way.
I can say the building is Class A with LEED certification.

practiceBank.title: Por que alugar nesta torre Class A
practiceBank.how: O aluno faz um pitch de 90s para convencer o cliente a fechar a locação: destaca 'efficiency', 'LEED certification', 'Class A building' e 'open floor plan'. O professor faz uma objeção no fim e o aluno responde na hora.

practiceBank.title: Perguntas do tenant sobre a planta
practiceBank.how: Professor e aluno alternam perguntas rápidas ('What's the net leasable area?', 'How efficient is the floor?'). O aluno responde curto e devolve pergunta. Treina fluência com os números e o vocab da aula.

practiceBank.title: De gross area para net leasable
practiceBank.how: O professor diz um valor de gross area e uma taxa de core. O aluno transforma oralmente em net leasable area e enuncia a 'efficiency' em inglês ('If gross is 1000 and core is 20%, net leasable is 800, so efficiency is 80%'). Repetição com números variados.

practiceBank.title: Fechando a locação em 8 minutos
practiceBank.how: Em 8 minutos, aluno (engenheiro/locador) e professor (tenant) negociam a locação da torre. O aluno usa 'to lease', 'to target', 'net leasable area' e defende o valor pela eficiência e padrão Class A. Foco em linguagem de negociação.

practiceBank.title: Open floor plan vs. salas fechadas
practiceBank.how: O professor defende salas fechadas; o aluno defende 'open floor plan' para o cliente corporativo, dando motivos (efficiency, flexibilidade, footprint). Cada um sustenta a posição em inglês. Produção argumentativa com o vocab da aula.

practiceBank.title: Resumo da torre em 60 segundos
practiceBank.how: O aluno grava 60s descrevendo a torre para um cliente: tipo de edifício (Class A), LEED certification, floor plate, efficiency e net leasable area. Deve encaixar ao menos 6 termos. O professor devolve 2 ajustes de clareza.

practiceBank.title: O aluno vira o cliente corporativo
practiceBank.how: O aluno assume o papel do tenant americano e o professor é o corretor. O aluno faz as perguntas que um cliente real faria sobre eficiência, área e certificação, em inglês. Treina o ponto de vista do cliente e o vocab no modo pergunta.

practiceBank.title: O que o tenant valoriza?
practiceBank.how: O aluno entrevista o professor (e/ou colegas imaginários) sobre o que mais importa numa torre (efficiency, LEED, localização) e depois reporta em inglês: 'Most tenants target Class A buildings because...'. Produz perguntas e síntese falada.

practiceBank.title: Defendendo a eficiência da planta
practiceBank.how: O aluno na cadeira quente recebe perguntas duras do professor (tenant) sobre por que a efficiency não é maior, o tamanho do core e o custo do net leasable. Responde sem travar, defendendo o projeto. Resposta rápida sob pressão.

pill.tip: Em datas, o dia leva som de ordinal com 'th': "third" (terceiro) e "fourth" (quarto). O 'th' é a língua entre os dentes, sem virar 'f' nem 's'.
pill.sample: The meeting moves from the third to the fourth of June.

lessons.title: Hospital construction & healthcare facilities
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você vai saber falar, em inglês simples, sobre construção de hospitais, sistemas críticos e segurança do paciente.
lessons.overview:
A healthcare facility is one of the hardest projects to build. A hospital is never just a building. It is a place where doctors save lives every day. The operating room and the ICU must work all the time. For Racional, a hospital project means very high quality and zero room for error.

The most important word in a hospital is safety. Patient safety comes first. Many systems are critical systems: they cannot stop. So the hospital has redundancy. This means we have a backup for every important part. If one power feed stops, a backup generator starts in seconds. The goal is high uptime, so the hospital does not fail.

A hospital also has special systems that other buildings do not have. There is medical gas for the patients. There is strong air filtration for infection control, to keep the air clean. All these systems must stay running during surgery. When Racional explains this to an American client, clear and simple English about safety builds trust fast.
lessons.intro:
Hoje você vai praticar como falar de sistemas críticos e segurança do paciente em um hospital. Frases-âncora: "Patient safety comes first.", "These systems must stay running." e "We have redundancy and a backup generator."

Use frases curtas e firmes. Em hospital, o tom é de segurança e confiança.
lessons.situation: Você acompanha o cliente americano em uma visita à obra de um hospital. Ele pergunta como você garante que os sistemas críticos não vão parar.
lessons.context: This is the operating room and this is the ICU. These are critical systems. They must stay running all the time. Patient safety comes first. We have redundancy here. If one power feed fails, the backup generator starts in seconds. We also have medical gas and strong air filtration for infection control. Our goal is high uptime.

vocab.example: This healthcare facility is very modern.
The operating room must always work.
The ICU is on this floor.
We have redundancy in every system.
We have two power feeds for safety.
Medical gas goes to every room.
The air filtration keeps the air clean.
The ICU is a critical system.

exercises.title: 1. Associe o termo em inglês ao significado em português
exercises.explanation: Quatro pilares do hospital: o lugar crítico (operating room), a proteção (redundancy), a meta maior (patient safety) e o indicador (uptime).

exercises.title: 2. Escreva sua resposta ao cliente
exercises.prompt: Escreva 2 frases curtas dizendo que os sistemas críticos do hospital não podem parar e que há gerador de emergência. Use ao menos 2 termos da aula em inglês.
exercises.modelAnswer: These critical systems must stay running. We have redundancy and a backup generator. Patient safety comes first.
exercises.explanation: A correção olha só o uso dos termos: mostre que você sabe falar de continuidade e segurança no hospital.

exercises.title: 3. Escolha a frase correta
exercises.prompt: O cliente pergunta o que acontece se a energia principal cair. O que você responde?

options.text: The operating room is closed.
options.whyWrong: Você quer mostrar continuidade, não fechar a sala de cirurgia.

options.text: The backup generator starts in seconds.
The system will fail.
options.whyWrong: Fail é falhar; isso passa a mensagem errada de insegurança.

exercises.title: 4. Coloque as palavras na ordem correta
exercises.explanation: Adjetivo antes do substantivo: "critical systems". Depois o verbo modal: "must stay running".

exercises.title: 5. Leia em voz alta
exercises.targetText: Patient safety comes first. These critical systems must stay running.
exercises.translation: A segurança do paciente vem primeiro. Estes sistemas críticos têm que continuar funcionando.
exercises.prompt: Você está na obra do hospital com o cliente. Fale com tom firme e seguro.
exercises.explanation: Duas frases curtas e fortes: o princípio (patient safety) e a regra técnica (stay running).

lessons.critical: Em voz alta, por 15 a 20 segundos, explique ao cliente que no hospital a segurança do paciente vem primeiro, que os sistemas críticos não podem parar e que há redundância com gerador de emergência. Use "patient safety", "critical system" e "backup generator".
takeaways: I can talk about a hospital and its critical systems.
I can say patient safety comes first.
I can explain redundancy and a backup generator.
I can say these systems must stay running.

practiceBank.how: O professor propõe um cenário: a 'power feed' principal falha durante uma cirurgia. O aluno explica em inglês como o 'backup generator' e a 'redundancy' garantem 'uptime' e que o sistema 'stays running'. Foco em explicar plano de contingência.

practiceBank.how: O professor descreve (ou mostra) um diagrama com operating room, ICU, medical gas, air filtration. O aluno descreve em inglês onde estão os 'critical systems' e como o 'infection control' e a 'air filtration' protegem o 'patient safety'.

practiceBank.title: Perguntas sobre segurança do paciente
practiceBank.how: Professor e aluno alternam perguntas rápidas ('What happens if a generator fails?', 'How do you keep the OR running?'). O aluno responde curto, usando 'redundancy', 'uptime', 'to fail', 'to stay running'. Ritmo e fluência.

practiceBank.how: O aluno grava 60s explicando ao cliente como o hospital mantém os sistemas críticos funcionando: redundancy, backup generator, power feed. Deve usar ao menos 6 termos. O professor devolve 2 ajustes.

practiceBank.how: O aluno ordena os critical systems (power feed, medical gas, air filtration, backup generator) do mais ao menos tolerante a downtime, justificando em inglês com base na 'patient safety'. O professor contesta a ordem para gerar mais fala.

pill.tip: Ao dizer a hora, soletre as letras: "a.m." soa 'êi-ÉM' e "p.m." soa 'pi-ÉM', com a tônica na segunda letra. Não diga como palavra única.

lessons.title: Shopping centers & retail
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você vai saber falar, em inglês simples, sobre shopping centers, lojas, fit-out e a abertura ao público.
lessons.overview:
A shopping center, or mall, is a large retail building with many stores. People go there to shop, to eat, and to spend time with family. Racional builds malls with a strong common area, a food court, and a large parking structure. The goal is to bring people in and keep them happy.

One key word is the anchor store. This is a big, famous store that pulls many people into the mall. More people means more footfall, and more footfall is good for every tenant. Each tenant gets an empty space and does the fit-out, which means they build their own store inside. The storefront is the front of the store, the part the client sees.

A mall has a hard schedule. The most important date is the grand opening, the day the mall opens to the public. To hit this date, Racional uses phasing: the team builds and opens the mall in parts. The contract manager must show the client that the project is on track and that Racional will hand over each area on time. A clean handover makes the grand opening a success.
lessons.intro:
Hoje você vai praticar como falar do shopping, das lojas e da abertura ao público. Frases-âncora: "The anchor store brings more footfall.", "The project is on track for the grand opening." e "We will hand over this area on time."

Use frases curtas e datas claras. Uma ideia por frase.
lessons.situation: Você apresenta o andamento da obra do shopping ao cliente americano. Ele quer confirmar a data da inauguração (grand opening) e o cronograma de entrega das lojas.
lessons.context: Welcome to our shopping center. This is the common area and this is the food court. The anchor store is here. It will bring a lot of footfall. Each tenant will do the fit-out of their store. The project is on track for the grand opening. We use phasing, so we open the mall in parts. We will hand over this area on time.

vocab.example: This shopping center is very large.
The anchor store is on the first floor.
Each tenant builds their own store.
The grand opening is in June.
The common area is clean and bright.
The food court is on this floor.
The anchor store brings more footfall.

We will hand over this area soon.

lessons.title: American sports (NFL, NBA, MLB, golf)
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você vai saber conversar, em inglês simples, sobre esportes americanos para criar conexão com o cliente.
lessons.overview:
In the United States, sports are everywhere. American people love to talk about their team. They watch games on TV with family and friends. For a Racional contract manager, a short talk about sports is a great way to break the ice with an American client and build a real connection.

The big sports are easy to know. Football (American football) is number one, and the biggest game is the Super Bowl. Basketball (the NBA) and baseball (the MLB) are also very popular. Golf is the sport for business: many deals start when two people play a round of golf together. Be careful: in the US, "football" means American football, and "soccer" means the game we call futebol in Brazil.

You do not need to be an expert. You just need a few simple phrases. You can ask, "Did you catch the game last night?" or "Who do you root for?" You can talk about the score, the playoffs, or a close game. A short, friendly talk before a meeting makes the American client feel at home and helps the long Racional project run more smoothly.
lessons.intro:
Hoje você vai praticar small talk sobre esportes para abrir uma conversa com o cliente americano. Frases-âncora: "Did you catch the game last night?", "Who do you root for?" e "It was a close game!"

Tom leve e amigável. Não precisa ser especialista, só puxar conversa.
lessons.situation: Antes de uma reunião, você quer quebrar o gelo com o cliente americano. Você sabe que ele gosta de futebol americano e que houve um jogo importante na noite anterior.
lessons.context: Hi! Did you catch the game last night? It was a close game! I like football too. Who do you root for? My team is not in the playoffs this year. Do you play golf? We can play a round of golf one day. I am a big fan of sports. The score was very close at the end.

vocab.example: Did you catch the game last night?
Football is very big in the US.
In the US, soccer means futebol.
The Super Bowl is the biggest game.
I am a big fan of golf.

vocab.en: to play a round of golf
vocab.example: Let's play a round of golf.
My team is in the playoffs.

exercises.explanation: Pergunta amigável + comentário curto: uma forma simples e natural de abrir conversa.

exercises.prompt: Escreva 2 frases curtas para puxar conversa sobre esportes com o cliente: pergunte se ele viu o jogo e por qual time torce. Use ao menos 2 termos da aula em inglês.
exercises.modelAnswer: Did you catch the game last night? It was a close game! Who do you root for? I am a big fan too.
exercises.explanation: A correção olha só o uso dos termos: mostre que você sabe abrir uma conversa leve sobre esportes.

lessons.critical: Em voz alta, por 15 a 20 segundos, quebre o gelo com o cliente americano: pergunte se ele viu o jogo, comente que foi um jogo apertado e pergunte por qual time ele torce. Use "catch the game", "close game" e "root for".
takeaways: I can start a conversation about American sports.
I can ask who someone roots for.
I can talk about the score and a close game.
I can invite a client to play a round of golf.

activities.title: The Super Bowl
activities.body:
The Super Bowl is the biggest game in American football. It happens one time every year, usually in February. Two teams play to win the championship. Millions of people watch the game on TV.

For many Americans, the Super Bowl is like a holiday. Families and friends meet at home. They eat pizza, chicken wings, and snacks. They watch the game together and cheer for their team.

The TV commercials are also famous. Companies pay a lot of money to show funny ads. The music show in the middle of the game is very popular too.

question.q: Qual opção resume melhor o texto?

options.text: The Super Bowl is the most important American football game of the year, and people watch it together with food, ads, and a music show.
The Super Bowl is a game where companies show funny TV commercials.
Americans love many sports and watch them on TV every day.
The Super Bowl is a holiday when families eat pizza and chicken wings.

activities.title: Basketball and the NBA
activities.body:
Basketball is a very popular sport in the United States. The best league is the NBA. Teams from many cities play games from October to June.

People love basketball because it is fast and exciting. Players run, jump, and shoot the ball into a high basket. Famous players like Michael Jordan and LeBron James are known all over the world.

Many people watch NBA games on TV or go to the arena. Fans wear shirts with the name and number of their favorite player. Talking about basketball is an easy way to start a conversation with an American friend.

question.q: Qual opção resume melhor o texto?

options.text: Basketball is a popular and exciting American sport, played in the NBA, with famous players and many fans.
Michael Jordan and LeBron James are the only two famous basketball players.
The NBA season starts in October and ends in June.
Americans like many sports and often wear team shirts.

activities.title: Baseball: America's Pastime
activities.body:
Baseball is one of the oldest sports in the United States. People call it "America's pastime." The main league is the MLB, with teams like the New York Yankees and the Boston Red Sox.

The game is slower than football or basketball. A player hits the ball with a bat and runs around four bases. Many families enjoy a calm afternoon at the stadium.

At the game, fans eat hot dogs and popcorn. They sing a famous song in the middle of the match. For Americans, baseball brings good memories of summer and family time.

question.q: Qual opção resume melhor o texto?

options.text: Baseball is an old, calm American sport played in the MLB that many families enjoy at the stadium with food and tradition.
Baseball is a sport where a player hits a ball with a bat and runs to four bases.
American sports are slow and families like to watch them in summer.
The New York Yankees and the Boston Red Sox are the best baseball teams.

lessons.title: Data centers (cooling, redundancy, Tier)
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você vai saber falar, em inglês simples, sobre data centers, resfriamento, redundância e Tier para clientes como Microsoft, Amazon e Google.
lessons.overview:
A data center is a building full of computers, called servers. These servers run the internet, the cloud, and big software. Racional builds hyperscale data centers for the largest clients in the world, like Microsoft, Amazon, and Google. Hyperscale means very, very large. This is one of the most important segments for Racional today.

A data center must never stop. The most important word is uptime. If the data center has downtime, the client loses a lot of money. So the building has a lot of redundancy. Engineers talk about N+1 or 2N: this means extra equipment, so there is always a backup. The UPS and the generators keep the power on if the city power goes down. They take over in seconds.

The servers make a lot of heat, so a strong cooling system is key. If the room gets too hot, the servers overheat and stop. The server room, also called white space, has a raised floor for cables and cold air. The load is the power the servers use. Clients also ask about the Tier level, like Tier III or Tier IV. A higher Tier means more safety and more uptime. Clear English about these systems is a must for the Racional contract manager.
lessons.intro:
Hoje você vai praticar como falar de resfriamento, redundância e Tier em um data center. Frases-âncora: "The cooling system keeps the servers cool.", "We have redundancy, so the system never goes down." e "This is a Tier IV data center."

Use frases curtas e termos técnicos simples. Uma ideia por frase.
lessons.situation: Você apresenta a obra de um data center hyperscale ao cliente americano (Microsoft, Amazon ou Google). Ele quer entender a redundância e o sistema de resfriamento.
lessons.context: This is a hyperscale data center. This is the server room, the white space. It has a raised floor for the cables and the cold air. The cooling system keeps the servers cool, so they do not overheat. We have a lot of redundancy here. This is a Tier IV building. If the city power goes down, the generators take over in seconds. Our goal is very high uptime.

vocab.example: This data center is very large.
The cooling system is very strong.
This is a Tier IV data center.
Our goal is very high uptime.
The system must not go down.
The generators take over in seconds.
The UPS keeps the power on.
The raised floor holds the cables.
The load is high in this room.

exercises.title: 1. Ouça e escreva a frase
exercises.correctText: The cooling system keeps the servers cool.
exercises.explanation: Frase-chave sobre o resfriamento, central na operação de um data center.

exercises.title: 2. Escolha a frase correta
exercises.prompt: O cliente pergunta o que acontece se a energia da cidade cair. O que você responde?

options.text: The servers overheat.
options.whyWrong: Superaquecer é problema de resfriamento, não de energia.

options.text: The generators take over in seconds.
The system goes down.
options.whyWrong: "Goes down" é cair; isso é o contrário do que você quer mostrar.

exercises.title: 3. Associe o termo em inglês ao significado em português
exercises.explanation: Quatro termos do data center: o calor (cooling system), a proteção (redundancy), a meta (uptime) e a estrutura (raised floor).

exercises.title: 4. Escreva sua resposta ao cliente
exercises.prompt: Escreva 2 frases curtas dizendo que o data center tem redundância e que o sistema nunca vai parar. Use ao menos 2 termos da aula em inglês.
exercises.modelAnswer: We have a lot of redundancy here. If the power goes down, the generators take over. Our goal is very high uptime.
exercises.explanation: A correção olha só o uso dos termos: mostre que você sabe falar de redundância e continuidade no data center.

exercises.title: 5. Leia em voz alta
exercises.targetText: This is a Tier IV data center. We have a lot of redundancy here.
exercises.translation: Este é um data center Tier IV. Temos muita redundância aqui.
exercises.prompt: Você está na obra do data center com o cliente da Microsoft, Amazon ou Google. Fale com tom técnico e seguro.
exercises.explanation: Duas ideias curtas: o nível do data center (Tier IV) e a proteção (redundancy).

lessons.critical: Em voz alta, por 15 a 20 segundos, apresente o data center ao cliente: diga que é um Tier IV hyperscale, que o sistema de resfriamento mantém os servidores frios e que há redundância para garantir alto uptime. Use "cooling system", "redundancy" e "uptime".
takeaways: I can describe a hyperscale data center to a client.
I can talk about the cooling system and overheating.
I can explain redundancy and Tier levels.
I can say the generators take over to keep high uptime.

lessons.title: Industrial facilities & manufacturing plants
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você descreve, em inglês simples, uma obra industrial — galpão, linha de produção, layout e fluxo de materiais — para conversar com o cliente sobre manufacturing plants.
lessons.overview:
An industrial facility is a building made for work and production. A manufacturing plant makes products. A warehouse stores them. These buildings look simple, but they are not. The floor must be very strong. The clear height must be high. The space must be open and flexible.

At Racional, industry is a key segment. We build big plants and large warehouses. We also build data centers for clients like Microsoft, Amazon, and Google. These projects need a strong industrial floor, a clear layout, and good material flow. The building must support heavy machines and trucks every day.

As a contract manager, you talk about these things with the client. You explain the building shell, the loading dock, and the production line. You use simple words to describe a complex building. This lesson gives you the basic vocabulary to do that with confidence.
lessons.intro:
Nesta aula você vai usar frases-âncora simples para descrever a obra industrial: "This is a manufacturing plant.", "The floor is heavy-duty." e "The layout keeps the material flow clear."

Pratique nomear as partes (shell, floor, loading dock) e dizer para que servem, em frases curtas no presente simples.
lessons.situation: Num tour de obra, um cliente norte-americano da indústria pergunta sobre o galpão e a linha de produção. Você descreve o espaço em inglês simples.
lessons.context: This is a manufacturing plant. The floor is very strong. It is heavy-duty. The clear height is high. Trucks come to the loading dock. The layout is open. This keeps the material flow easy. We want to keep the line moving every day.

vocab.example: This is a big industrial facility.

lessons.title: Procurement & sourcing
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você fala, em inglês simples, sobre compras e contratação na obra — procurement, cotação, fornecedores e seleção — para conversar com o cliente sobre sourcing.
lessons.overview:
Procurement means buying. Sourcing means finding the right supplier. On a big project, this is a key job. We need steel, concrete, glass, and many systems. We must buy them at the right price and at the right time. Good procurement protects the cost and the schedule.

At Racional, the team sends an RFQ to many suppliers. The RFQ asks for a price. Each supplier sends a quote. We compare the quotes. We do not always pick the lowest price. We pick the best value. For a Microsoft or Amazon data center, quality and lead time are very important.

As a contract manager, you talk about procurement with the client. You explain the shortlist, the scope of supply, and the cost saving. When the choice is clear, we award the contract and send a purchase order. This lesson gives you the words to do that in English.
lessons.intro:
Nesta aula você usa frases simples de compras: "We send an RFQ to three suppliers.", "We compare the quotes." e "We award the contract to the best value."

Pratique descrever os passos: pedir cotação, comparar, escolher e emitir o pedido de compra (purchase order).
lessons.situation: Numa reunião de status, o cliente americano quer saber como a Racional escolhe os fornecedores. Você explica o processo de procurement em inglês simples.
lessons.context: Our procurement process is clear. First, we send an RFQ to three suppliers. Each supplier sends a quote. We compare the quotes. We do not always pick the lowest price. We pick the best value. Then we award the contract and send a purchase order. We watch the lead time, because it protects the schedule.

vocab.example: The procurement team buys the steel.
This supplier is fast and reliable.
We send an RFQ to three suppliers.
I send the purchase order now.
We pick the best value, not the lowest price.
The lead time is six weeks.
We negotiate the price and the date.
The scope of supply is clear in the quote.
We have three suppliers on the shortlist.
We compare quotes before we decide.
This choice is a real cost saving.

exercises.title: 1. Ouça e escreva
exercises.correctText: We send an RFQ to three suppliers.
exercises.explanation: "RFQ" é o pedido de cotação. Pronuncie cada letra: R-F-Q.

exercises.title: 2. Coloque na ordem certa
exercises.explanation: Ordem básica: sujeito (We) + verbo (compare) + objeto (the quotes).

exercises.title: 3. Complete a frase
exercises.prompt: We do not pick the lowest price. We pick the ___.
exercises.explanation: "Best value" é o melhor custo-benefício, não o preço mais baixo.

exercises.title: 4. Escolha a resposta correta
exercises.prompt: O cliente pergunta o próximo passo depois de escolher o fornecedor. O que você diz?

options.text: We award the contract and send a purchase order.
We send an RFQ to the supplier.
options.whyWrong: O RFQ vem antes, no início do processo.

options.text: We compare the quotes again.
options.whyWrong: A comparação já aconteceu; o fornecedor já foi escolhido.

exercises.title: 5. Leia em voz alta
exercises.targetText: We compare the quotes. Then we award the contract.
exercises.translation: Nós comparamos as cotações. Depois adjudicamos o contrato.
exercises.prompt: Você explica o processo ao cliente. Leia as duas frases com clareza.
exercises.explanation: "Award" soa como "a-uórd". Faça uma pausa após "quotes".

lessons.critical: Em voz alta, por 15-20 segundos, explique ao cliente como a Racional compra: como você pede cotação, compara as quotes e escolhe o best value, não o menor preço.
takeaways: I can explain our procurement process.
I can send an RFQ and compare quotes.
I can pick the best value, not the lowest price.
I can award a contract and send a purchase order.

practiceBank.how: O aluno faz o papel do cliente americano cético e o professor é o comprador. O aluno pergunta por que tal supplier foi escolhido, cobra cost saving e best value, e força o professor a justificar a shortlist. Depois trocam.

practiceBank.how: Cenário: o quote mais barato tem lead time que estoura o prazo da obra. O aluno explica ao cliente, em inglês, como resolver — renegociar, mudar scope of supply ou trocar de vendor. Professor levanta o trade-off custo x prazo.

practiceBank.title: Pesquise os critérios de fornecedor
practiceBank.how: O aluno entrevista o professor sobre como uma empresa americana faz sourcing (perguntas em inglês sobre RFQ, best value, negotiate). Depois reporta de volta em 3-4 frases as diferenças com a Racional. Professor fornece respostas variadas.

practiceBank.title: Do passado para o presente do processo
practiceBank.how: O professor diz uma frase ('We awarded the contract last week') e o aluno a transforma (planejado, em andamento, futuro) mantendo o vocab de procurement. Foco em soar natural ao falar de quotes, POs e lead times. Ritmo rápido.

pill.tip: Para soar educado, use "could you" (cud iú) com entonação suave, sem cair como uma ordem reta. Um leve toque ascendente no fim transmite cortesia.

lessons.title: Imports, lead times & containers
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você fala, em inglês simples, sobre importação de materiais — prazos de entrega, containers e atrasos de logística — para alinhar expectativas de prazo com o cliente.
lessons.overview:
Some materials come from other countries. We import them. They travel by sea, inside a container. The ship goes to a port. Then the material must clear customs. All of this takes time. The total time is the lead time.

At Racional, imports are common on big projects. A data center for Amazon or Google may need special equipment from abroad. We place an order early. We work with a freight forwarder. We watch the supply chain every week. A long lead time can be a real risk for the schedule.

As a contract manager, you must explain this to the client. You talk about shipping, customs clearance, and possible delay. You add a buffer to protect the schedule. This lesson gives you the words to align dates with the client in English.
lessons.intro:
Nesta aula você usa frases simples de importação: "We import this material by sea.", "The lead time is ten weeks." e "We add a buffer to protect the schedule."

Pratique falar de prazos, containers e do risco de atraso na alfândega (customs).
lessons.situation: O cliente americano quer saber por que um equipamento demora a chegar. Você explica a importação e o prazo em inglês simples.
lessons.context: This equipment comes from abroad. We import it by sea, in a container. The ship goes to the port of Santos. Then the material must clear customs. The total lead time is ten weeks. So we place the order early. We add a buffer. This protects the schedule.

vocab.example: The lead time is ten weeks.
Shipping by sea is slower but cheaper.
The parts travel in one container.
The ship arrives at the port.
A delay at customs is a risk.
We add a buffer to the date.
We watch the supply chain every week.
Our freight forwarder books the ship.
A buffer helps protect the schedule.

exercises.title: 1. Ligue o termo à tradução
exercises.explanation: Quatro termos centrais para falar de importação e prazo.

exercises.title: 2. Escreva ao cliente
exercises.prompt: Explique em 2 frases curtas por que o equipamento demora. Use ao menos 2 termos da aula (em inglês), como import, lead time, by sea, customs ou buffer.
exercises.modelAnswer: We import this equipment by sea. The lead time is ten weeks. We add a buffer to protect the schedule.
exercises.explanation: A correção é só sobre o uso dos termos da aula. Use o presente simples.

exercises.title: 3. Escolha a resposta correta
exercises.prompt: O cliente teme um atraso. Como você diz que se protegeu disso?

options.text: We add a buffer to protect the schedule.
We import the schedule by sea.
options.whyWrong: Não se importa um cronograma; importa-se o material.

options.text: We clear the buffer at customs.
options.whyWrong: Quem passa pela alfândega é o material, não o buffer.

exercises.title: 4. Coloque na ordem certa
exercises.explanation: "Place an order" = fazer um pedido. O advérbio "early" vem no fim.

exercises.title: 5. Leia em voz alta
exercises.targetText: The lead time is long. We place the order early.
exercises.translation: O prazo de entrega é longo. Nós fazemos o pedido cedo.
exercises.prompt: Você tranquiliza o cliente sobre o prazo. Leia com calma.
exercises.explanation: "Lead" soa como "líd". Faça uma pausa entre as duas frases.

lessons.critical: Em voz alta, por 15-20 segundos, explique ao cliente a importação de um equipamento: diga que vem por mar, qual o lead time, o risco na alfândega e como você usa um buffer para proteger o cronograma.
takeaways: I can talk about imports in English.
I can explain lead time and shipping by sea.
I can talk about customs and possible delays.
I can say we add a buffer to protect the schedule.

pill.region: Evitar fillers — pausar em vez de 'uh'
pill.tip: Em vez de encher com 'uh'/'um', faça uma pausa silenciosa. Troque o vício por uma muleta limpa como "let me check" (lét mi tchék) enquanto pensa.
pill.sample: Let me check the numbers and get back to you.

lessons.title: Personal hobbies & sports (cycling, swimming, walking)
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você conversa, em inglês simples, sobre seus hobbies e esportes favoritos — pedalar, nadar, caminhar — usando isso para criar vínculo com o cliente fora da reunião formal.
lessons.overview:
Work is not the only topic with a client. People also talk about life. They talk about hobbies and sports. This is called small talk. It builds a real connection. A good relationship makes the whole project easier.

Many people enjoy simple sports. They like cycling, swimming, or just to go for a walk. They do it on the weekend, outdoors, in the fresh air. It helps them relax and stay in shape. These are easy and friendly topics.

At Racional, a project with Microsoft or Amazon can last 18 to 24 months. That is a long time. You meet the same people again and again. Small talk about a hobby helps you build trust. This lesson gives you simple words to connect with the client like a person, not only like a manager.
lessons.intro:
Nesta aula você usa frases leves e pessoais: "I like cycling on the weekend.", "I swim twice a week." e "It helps me relax."

Pratique falar do que você gosta de fazer no tempo livre, com tom amigável e descontraído.
lessons.situation: Antes da reunião começar, o cliente americano pergunta o que você faz nos fins de semana. Você puxa papo sobre seus hobbies em inglês simples.
lessons.context: On the weekend, I like to stay active. I enjoy cycling. I ride my bike outdoors. I also swim twice a week. Sometimes I just go for a walk in the fresh air. It helps me relax and clear my head. What about you? What do you like to do?

vocab.example: I ride my bike every Sunday.
Swimming is good for my back.
I go for a walk after lunch.
I work out twice a week.
I exercise to stay in shape.
A walk helps me clear my head.
I ride my bike on the weekend.
I enjoy walking in the park.
I love the fresh air outdoors.

exercises.title: 1. Ligue o termo à tradução
exercises.explanation: Quatro termos leves para falar de hobbies e esportes.

exercises.title: 2. Escolha a resposta natural

options.text: I enjoy cycling. It helps me relax.
I award the contract on the weekend.
options.whyWrong: Isso é vocabulário de trabalho, não de hobby.

options.text: I import a bike twice a week.
options.whyWrong: "Import" é de logística; aqui você só fala do hobby.

exercises.title: 3. Leia em voz alta
exercises.targetText: I enjoy cycling. I ride my bike outdoors. It helps me relax.
exercises.translation: Eu gosto de pedalar. Ando de bicicleta ao ar livre. Isso me ajuda a relaxar.
exercises.prompt: Imagine o papo leve antes da reunião. Leia com tom descontraído.
exercises.explanation: Sorria ao falar; o tom amigável importa tanto quanto as palavras.

exercises.title: 4. Escreva sobre você
exercises.prompt: Conte em 2 frases curtas o que você gosta de fazer no tempo livre. Use ao menos 2 termos da aula (em inglês), como cycling, swimming, go for a walk, weekend ou relax.
exercises.modelAnswer: On the weekend, I enjoy cycling. I ride my bike outdoors. Sometimes I go for a walk. It helps me relax.
exercises.explanation: A correção é só sobre o uso dos termos da aula. Tom pessoal e leve é o ideal.

takeaways: I can talk about my hobbies in English.
I can say I enjoy cycling and swimming.
I can ask the client about their free time.
I can use small talk to build a connection.
